entries.title: Algebra
entries.body: **Algebra** is the branch of mathematics that studies symbols and the rules for manipulating them.

entries.title: Set
entries.body: A **set** is a collection of distinct objects.

entries.title: Subset
entries.body: \(A\subseteq B\) means every element of \(A\) also belongs to \(B\).

entries.title: Group
entries.body: A **group** is \((G,\ast)\) with closure, associativity, identity, and inverses.

entries.title: Cyclic Group
entries.body: A group is **cyclic** if generated by a single element: \(G=\langle g\rangle\).

entries.title: Homomorphism
entries.body: A map \(\varphi:G\to H\) is a **group homomorphism** if \(\varphi(x\ast y)=\varphi(x)\star\varphi(y)\).

entries.title: Subgroup
entries.body: A **subgroup** \(H\subseteq G\) is a group under the inherited operation.

entries.title: Ring
entries.body: A **ring** has two operations, with addition forming an abelian group and multiplication distributing over addition.

entries.title: Commutative Ring
entries.body: A ring is **commutative** if multiplication is commutative: \(ab=ba\).

entries.title: Field
entries.body: A **field** is a commutative ring where every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

entries.title: Characteristic of a Field
entries.body: The **characteristic** is the smallest positive \(n\) such that \(n\cdot 1=0\), or \(0\) if no such \(n\) exists.

entries.title: Natural Numbers
entries.body: \(\mathbb N\) typically denotes nonnegative integers or positive integers depending on convention.

entries.title: Integers
entries.body: \(\mathbb Z\) is the set of whole numbers including negatives.

entries.title: Integral Domain
entries.body: A commutative ring with identity and no zero divisors.

entries.title: Rationals, Reals, Complexes
entries.body: \(\mathbb Q\subset\mathbb R\subset\mathbb C\).

entries.title: Divides
entries.body: \(a\mid b\) means there exists \(k\in\mathbb Z\) such that \(b=ka\).

entries.title: Greatest Common Divisor
entries.body: \(\gcd(a,b)\) is the largest positive integer dividing both \(a\) and \(b\).

entries.title: Coprime
entries.body: Integers \(a,b\) are **coprime** if \(\gcd(a,b)=1\).

entries.title: Congruence
entries.body: \(a\equiv b\pmod n\iff n\mid(a-b)\).

entries.title: Modulo Class
entries.body: A **congruence class** modulo \(n\) contains numbers with the same remainder mod \(n\).

entries.title: Modular Inverse
entries.body: For \(a\), the modular inverse \(a^{-1}\) (mod \(n\)) satisfies \(aa^{-1}\equiv1\pmod n\).

entries.title: Equation
entries.body: An **equation** is a statement \(LHS=RHS\).

entries.title: Identity
entries.body: An identity \(f(x)=g(x)\) holds for all values in domain, not just one solution.

entries.title: Polynomial Equation
entries.body: Equation where terms are polynomials: \(p(x)=0\).

entries.title: Function
entries.body: A **function** \(f:X\to Y\) maps each \(x\in X\) to one image in \(Y\).

entries.title: Injection
entries.body: A function \(f\) is injective if \(f(a)=f(b)\Rightarrow a=b\).

entries.title: Surjection
entries.body: A function \(f\) is surjective if every element of codomain has a preimage.

entries.title: Bijection
entries.body: A function is **bijective** if it is injective and surjective.

entries.title: Isomorphism
entries.body: An isomorphism is a bijective structure-preserving map.

entries.title: Equivalence Relation
entries.body: Relation \(\sim\) is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

entries.title: Equivalence Class
entries.body: For \(a\in S\), \([a]=\{x\in S\mid x\sim a\}\).

entries.title: Polynomial
entries.body: A polynomial in \(x\): \(\sum_{k=0}^n a_kx^k\), with \(a_n\neq 0\).

entries.title: Leading Coefficient
entries.body: In \(a_nx^n+\cdots+a_0\), coefficient \(a_n\) is the leading coefficient.

entries.title: Constant Term
entries.body: The term with exponent \(0\): \(a_0\).

entries.title: Degree
entries.body: Degree is the largest exponent with nonzero coefficient.

entries.title: Multiplicity of a Root
entries.body: The **multiplicity** of root \(r\) is the largest \(m\) such that \((x-r)^m\) divides the polynomial.

entries.title: Factorization
entries.body: A rewrite into a product of simpler expressions.

entries.title: Quadratic Formula
entries.body: Roots of \(ax^2+bx+c=0\): \(\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\).

entries.title: Rational Expression
entries.body: A quotient \(\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\) with \(q(x)\neq 0\).

entries.title: Rational Function
entries.body: A function that is a ratio of two polynomials.

entries.title: Domain Restriction
entries.body: A rational expression excludes zeros of denominator from its domain.

entries.title: Absolute Value
entries.body: \(|x| = \begin{cases}x,&x\ge0\\-x,&x<0\end{cases}\).

entries.title: AM-GM Inequality
entries.body: For nonnegative reals \(a,b\): \(\sqrt{ab}\le \frac{a+b}{2}\).

entries.title: Permutation
entries.body: A bijection from a set to itself.

entries.title: Transposition
entries.body: A permutation that swaps two elements and leaves others fixed.

entries.title: Symmetric Group
entries.body: \(S_n\) is the group of all permutations of \(\{1,\dots,n\}\).

entries.title: Orbit
entries.body: For action \(G\curvearrowright X\), orbit of \(x\) is \(\{g\cdot x:g\in G\}\).

entries.title: Equivalence-Preserving Manipulation
entries.body: Algebraic steps that maintain logical equivalence.

entries.title: Contradiction
entries.body: Assume \(\neg P\), derive contradiction, conclude \(P\).

entries.title: Function Composition
entries.body: \((g\circ f)(x)=g(f(x))\).

entries.title: Substitution
entries.body: Replace a variable with an equal expression to simplify or reframe an equation.

entries.title: Bézout Identity
entries.body:
For integers \(a,b\in\mathbb Z\), there exist \(x,y\in\mathbb Z\) such that
\[
ax+by=\gcd(a,b).
\]

entries.title: Remainder Theorem
entries.body: For polynomial \(p(x)\), \((x-c)\mid p(x)\) iff \(p(c)=0\).

entries.title: Lagrange's Theorem for Finite Groups
entries.body: If \(G\) is a finite group and \(H\le G\), then \(|H|\) divides \(|G|\).

entries.title: Unique Factorization in \(\mathbb Z\)
entries.body:
Every integer \(n>1\) has a factorization
\[
 n=p_1^{\alpha_1}p_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots p_k^{\alpha_k},
\]
where \(p_i\) are prime and this expression is unique up to ordering.

entries.title: Bézout via Euclidean Algorithm
entries.body:
Compute \(\gcd(48,18)\):
\[
48=2\cdot 18+12,\quad 18=1\cdot 12+6,\quad 12=2\cdot 6.
\]
So \(\gcd(48,18)=6\).
From back substitution:
\[
6=18-12=18-(48-2\cdot 18)=3\cdot 18-1\cdot 48.
\]
Hence \(6=3\cdot 18+(-1)\cdot 48\).

entries.title: Subgroup in Cyclic Group
entries.body:
In \(\mathbb Z_8\), generated element \(1\) gives
\(\langle 1\rangle=\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}=\mathbb Z_8\).
So \(\mathbb Z_8\) is cyclic; any subgroup order divides 8 (1,2,4,8).

entries.title: Q1. Find \(\gcd(48,18)\) and a Bézout representation.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Use the Euclidean algorithm:
\[
48 = 2\cdot18 + 12,
\]
\[
18 = 1\cdot12 + 6,
\]
\[
12 = 2\cdot6 + 0.
\]
So \(\gcd(48,18)=6\).
Back-substitute to write \(6\) as a combination of \(48\) and \(18\):
\[
6=18-1\cdot12
=18-(48-2\cdot18)=3\cdot18-1\cdot48.
\]
Hence \(6=3\cdot18+(-1)\cdot48\), a valid Bézout form.

entries.title: Q2. Factor \(p(x)=x^3-6x^2+11x-6\) into linear factors.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Evaluate at \(x=1\):
\[
p(1)=1-6+11-6=0.
\]
So \((x-1)\mid p(x)\). Perform synthetic division (or polynomial division):
\[
p(x)=(x-1)(x^2-5x+6).
\]
Then
\[
x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3).
\]
Therefore
\[
p(x)=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3).
\]

entries.title: Q3. Show that in \(\mathbb Z_8\), the element \([2]\) generates a subgroup of size 4.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Compute repeated multiples under addition modulo 8:
\[
[0],[2],[4],[6],[0],\dots
\]
There are 4 distinct elements before returning to \([0]\): \([0],[2],[4],[6]\).
Hence \(\langle [2]\rangle=\{[0],[2],[4],[6]\}\), so this subgroup has order 4. This also matches Lagrange’s theorem: 4 divides \(8\).

entries.title: Q4. Prove \((x-2)\mid x^3-6x^2+11x-6\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** By the remainder theorem, \((x-c)\mid p(x)\) iff \(p(c)=0\).
Set \(c=2\):
\[
p(2)=8-24+22-6=0.
\]
Thus \((x-2)\) divides the polynomial.

entries.title: Q5. Prove that the quotient of two nonzero rational numbers is rational.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Let \(a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Z\) with \(a/b\neq 0\), \(c/d\neq 0\), and \(b,d\neq 0\).
Then
\[
\frac{a/b}{c/d}=\frac{a}{b}\cdot\frac{d}{c}=\frac{ad}{bc}.
\]
Since \(ad\in\mathbb Z\) and \(bc\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\), the result is rational by definition.

entries.title: Q6. Show that \(\sqrt{2}\) is irrational.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Assume for contradiction \(\sqrt2\) is rational. Then \(\sqrt2=\frac{p}{q}\) with \(\gcd(p,q)=1\), \(q>0\).
Squaring gives:
\[
2=\frac{p^2}{q^2},\quad p^2=2q^2.
\]
So \(p^2\) is even, hence \(p\) even, so \(p=2k\).
Then
\[
(2k)^2=2q^2\Rightarrow 2k^2=q^2,
\]
so \(q^2\) even and \(q\) even. Contradiction because \(p,q\) cannot both be even while coprime. Therefore \(\sqrt2\) irrational.

entries.title: Q8. Verify \((\mathbb Z,+)\) is a group while \((\mathbb N,+)\) is not.
entries.body:
**Answer.** 
- In \((\mathbb Z,+)\), associativity and identity \(0\) hold; every integer \(n\) has inverse \(-n\in\mathbb Z\).
- In \((\mathbb N,+)\) with \(\mathbb N\) nonnegative, additivity and associativity hold but negatives are absent. For example, inverse of \(1\) would require \(-1\notin\mathbb N\).
Hence \((\mathbb Z,+)\) is a group and \((\mathbb N,+)\) is not.

entries.title: Euclidean Division Algorithm for Integers
entries.body:
For integers \(a\) and positive integer \(b\), there exist unique integers \(q,r\) such that
\[
a = bq + r,\quad 0 \le r < b.
\]

entries.title: Rational Root Theorem
entries.body:
If \(p(x)=a_nx^n+\cdots+a_0\in\mathbb Z[x]\) with \(a_n\neq 0\), and \(\frac{p}{q}\in\mathbb Q\) (in lowest terms) is a root of \(p\), then
\[p\mid a_0 \text{ and } q\mid a_n.\]

entries.title: Chinese Remainder Theorem for Two Moduli
entries.body:
If \(m,n\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(\gcd(m,n)=1\), then for any integers \(a,b\), the system
\[
x\equiv a\pmod m,\quad x\equiv b\pmod n
\]
has a solution, and the solution is unique modulo \(mn\).

entries.title: Lagrange Interpolation
entries.body: Given distinct nodes \((x_i,y_i)\in\mathbb F^2\), \(i=0,\dots,n\), with \(x_i\neq x_j\) for \(i\neq j\), there exists a unique polynomial \(p\in\mathbb F[x]\) with \(\deg p\le n\) such that \(p(x_i)=y_i\) for all \(i\).

entries.title: Unique Factorization of Polynomials over a Field
entries.body: Every nonzero polynomial \(p\in F[x]\) over a field \(F\) factors uniquely (up to ordering and multiplication by units) into irreducible polynomials.

entries.title: Q1. Euclidean Division (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Let \(a\in\mathbb Z\), \(b\in\mathbb N\). Define \(S=\{a-bq\mid q\in\mathbb Z,\ a-bq\ge 0\}\). Set \(S\) is nonempty and bounded below by 0, so by the Well-Ordering Principle it has minimum \(r\).
Then write \(a=bq+r\). If \(r\ge b\), then \(r-b\ge 0\) and \(r-b\in S\), contradicting minimality. So \(0\le r<b\).
If there were two such pairs \((q,r)\neq(q',r')\), then \(b(q-q')=r'-r\) with \(|r'-r|<b\) and \(b\mid(r'-r)\), forcing \(r=r'\), so \(q=q'\).

entries.title: Q2. Rational Root Theorem (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Suppose \(p(x)=a_nx^n+\cdots+a_0\) and \(\frac{p}{q}\) is a reduced root (\(\gcd(p,q)=1\)). Then
\[
0=p\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)=a_n\frac{p^n}{q^n}+\cdots+a_0
\]
Multiply by \(q^n\):
\[
 a_np^n + a_{n-1}p^{n-1}q+\cdots+a_1pq^{n-1}+a_0q^n=0.
\]
Rearrange
\[
 a_0q^n = -p(a_np^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1q^{n-1}).
\]
So \(p\mid a_0q^n\). Since \(\gcd(p,q)=1\), \(\gcd(p, q^n)=1\), thus \(p\mid a_0\).
Similarly
\[
 a_np^n = -q(a_{n-1}p^{n-1}q^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0q^{n-1}),
\]
so \(q\mid a_np^n\), hence \(q\mid a_n\).

entries.title: Q3. Chinese Remainder (Two-Moduli Form) (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Set \(x = a + m t\). Congruence \(x\equiv b\pmod n\) becomes
\[
a+mt\equiv b\pmod n \iff m t\equiv b-a\pmod n.
\]
Since \(\gcd(m,n)=1\), multiply both sides by inverse of \(m\) mod \(n\) to solve for \(t\) modulo \(n\), so solution exists and is unique mod \(n\). Then \(x=a+mt\) is unique mod \(mn\).

entries.title: Q4. Lagrange Interpolation (Existence and uniqueness)
entries.body:
Define basis polynomials
\[
L_i(x)=\prod_{j\ne i}\frac{x-x_j}{x_i-x_j},\quad i=0,\dots,n.
\]
Each \(L_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}\). Then
\[
p(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n y_iL_i(x)
\]
gives \(p(x_i)=y_i\). Each \(L_i\) has degree \(n\), so \(\deg p\le n\).
For uniqueness: if \(q\) another polynomial of degree \(\le n\) satisfies same data, then \(r=p-q\) has at least \(n+1\) roots \(x_0,\dots,x_n\), so\(r\equiv 0\), thus \(p=q\).

entries.title: Q5. Factorization in \(F[x]\) (Proof sketch)
entries.body: Because \(F[x]\) is a Euclidean domain, it is a unique factorization domain (UFD). Every nonzero nonunit in a UFD factors into irreducibles and factorization is unique up to order and units. Therefore every polynomial admits unique factorization as claimed.

entries.body: a ring element \\(x\in R\\) for which \\(x^n=0\\) for some positive integer \\(n\\).

entries.title: Noetherian Ring
entries.body: a ring in which every ascending chain of ideals stabilizes; equivalently every ideal is finitely generated.

entries.title: Principal Ideal Domain
entries.body: a domain in which every ideal is principal, i.e., of the form \((a)\) for some \(a\).

entries.title: Euclidean Domain
entries.body: a domain equipped with a norm \(N:R\setminus\{0\}\to \mathbb N\) such that division with remainder holds.

entries.title: Irreducible Element
entries.body: a nonzero nonunit \(a\in R\) where \(a=bc\) implies either \(b\) or \(c\) is a unit.

entries.title: Maximal Ideal
entries.body: a proper ideal \(M\subsetneq R\) such that there is no ideal strictly between \(M\) and \(R\).

entries.title: Dedekind Domain
entries.body: A Noetherian, integrally closed integral domain in which every nonzero prime ideal is maximal.

entries.title: Unique Factorization Domain
entries.body: An integral domain where each nonzero nonunit factors uniquely (up to order and units) into irreducibles.

entries.title: Fraction Field
entries.body: For an integral domain \(R\), its **fraction field** \(\mathrm{Frac}(R)\) is the smallest field containing \(R\), with elements \(a/b\).

entries.title: Localization
entries.body: Given a multiplicative set \(S\subseteq R\), the localization \(S^{-1}R\) is the ring of formal fractions \(a/s\) with \(a\in R,\;s\in S\), where elements of \(S\) become units.

entries.title: Radical Ideal
entries.body:
The radical of \(I\subseteq R\) is

\]

entries.body:

$\mathbb F\subseteq\mathbb E$, where

$\mathbb E/\mathbb F$, the **degree** is

$p(x)$ over 


$\mathbb F$ is the smallest field extension where 


$p\) splits into linear factors.

entries.title: Category
entries.body: A **category** consists of objects and morphisms where morphisms compose associatively and each object has an identity morphism.

entries.title: Functor
entries.body: A **functor** sends objects and morphisms from one category to another, preserving identities and composition.

entries.title: Natural Transformation
entries.body: A **natural transformation** is a family of morphisms between two functors that commutes with all morphisms in the source category.

entries.title: Adjunction
entries.body:
An **adjunction** between categories is data \((F\dashv G)\) with a natural bijection
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(A),B)\cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,G(B)).
\]

entries.title: Yoneda Lemma
entries.body:
For object \(X\) in locally small \(\mathcal C\), evaluation at \(X\) identifies
\[
\operatorname{Nat}(\operatorname{Hom}(X,-),F)\cong F(X)
\]
naturally in every functor \(F\).

entries.title: Ideal
entries.body: An **ideal** \(I\subset R\) of a commutative ring \(R\) is a subset closed under addition and under multiplication by elements of \(R\).

entries.title: Prime Ideal
entries.body: An ideal \(\mathfrak p\subset R\) is **prime** if \(ab\in\mathfrak p\) implies \(a\in\mathfrak p\) or \(b\in\mathfrak p\).

entries.title: Nilradical
entries.body:
The **nilradical** of \(R\) is
\[
\sqrt{(0)}=\{a\in R:a^n=0\text{ for some }n\in\mathbb N\}.
\]

entries.title: Prime Spectrum
entries.body: The **prime spectrum** \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) is the set of prime ideals of \(R\) with Zariski topology.

entries.title: Radical Ideal
entries.body:
For ideal \(I\), the **radical** is
\[
\sqrt I=\{a\in R: a^n\in I\text{ for some }n\in\mathbb N\}.
\]

entries.title: Short Exact Sequence
entries.body:
A sequence

a \xrightarrow{f} b \xrightarrow{g} c\n is **exact** iff 
\[
\mathrm{im}(f)=\ker(g).
\]

entries.title: Split Exact Sequence
entries.body:
A short exact sequence is **split** if it is isomorphic to
\(0\to A\to A\oplus C\to C\to 0\), so the middle term decomposes as a direct sum.

entries.title: Derived Functor
entries.body: For a functor \(F\), its derived functors \(R^iF\) measure failure of exactness, e.g.\(R^iF(X)=0\) for injective resolutions when \(F\) is exact.

entries.title: Projective Object
entries.body: An object \(P\) is **projective** if \(\mathrm{Hom}(P,-)\) is exact; equivalently every epimorphism \(f:P\twoheadrightarrow X\) lifts through surjections.

entries.title: Yoneda Extension Group
entries.body:
\(
\mathrm{Ext}^1(A,B)\) classifies short exact sequences
\(0\to B\to E\to A\to 0\) up to equivalence.

entries.title: Projective Resolution
entries.body:
A **projective resolution** of an object \(A\) is an exact sequence
\[
\cdots \to P_2 \to P_1 \to P_0 \to A \to 0
\]
where each \(P_i\) is projective.

entries.title: Tor Functor
entries.body: For modules \(M,N\),\(\mathrm{Tor}_n^R(M,N)\) is the left-derived functor of tensor; it measures failure of exactness of \(\otimes\).

entries.title: Derived Category
entries.body: The derived category \(D(A)\) is obtained from chain complexes by formally inverting quasi-isomorphisms.

entries.title: Flat Module
entries.body: A module \(M\) is **flat** if tensoring with it preserves exact sequences.

entries.title: Ext in Degree One
entries.body:
\(\mathrm{Ext}^1_R(M,N)\) classifies equivalence classes of short exact sequences
\(0\to N\to E\to M\to 0\).

entries.title: Exact Functor
entries.body: A functor \(F\) is **exact** if it preserves exact sequences; equivalently, exactness of \(0\to A\to B\to C\to 0\) implies exactness of \(0\to F(A)\to F(B)\to F(C)\to 0\).

entries.title: Noetherian Module
entries.body: A module \(M\) is **Noetherian** if every ascending chain of submodules stabilizes.

entries.title: Artinian Module
entries.body: A module \(M\) is **Artinian** if every descending chain of submodules stabilizes.

entries.title: Composition Series
entries.body:
A finite filtration
\[
0=M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_n=M
\]
with simple factors \(M_i/M_{i-1}\) is a composition series.

entries.title: Jordan--Hölder Multiset
entries.body: In a finite-length module, the multiset of composition factors is uniquely determined up to isomorphism and order.

entries.title: Adjunction
entries.body:
A pair \((F,G)\) is an **adjunction** \(F\dashv G\) if there is a natural bijection
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,G B)
\]
for objects \(A\in\mathcal C\), \(B\in\mathcal D\).

entries.title: Unit of Adjunction
entries.body: An adjunction has natural maps \(\eta: \mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal C}\to G F\) and \(\varepsilon: F G\to \mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal D}\).

entries.title: Representable Functor
entries.body: A functor \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}\) is representable if \(F\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)\) for some \(A\in\mathcal C\).

entries.title: Yoneda Embedding
entries.body:
The assignment \(X\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(X,-)\) defines a fully faithful functor
\(\mathcal C\to[\mathcal C,\mathbf{Set}]\).

entries.title: Torsion Pair
entries.body: A pair \((\mathcal T,\mathcal F)\) with \(\mathrm{Hom}(T,F)=0\) for \(T\in\mathcal T,F\in\mathcal F\), closed under extension in an abelian context.

entries.title: Projective Limit
entries.body:
The **projective limit** of a system \((A_i, f_{ij})\) is
\[
\varprojlim_i A_i = \left\{(a_i)\in\prod_i A_i\;\big|\;f_{ij}(a_j)=a_i\text{ for }i\le j\right\}.
\]

entries.title: Inductive Limit
entries.body: The **inductive limit** \(\varinjlim A_i\) is the universal object receiving compatible maps from all \(A_i\).

entries.title: Exactness of filtered colimits
entries.body: A filtered colimit of short exact sequences is exact in modules (equivalently, filtered colimits are exact in \(\mathbf{Mod}_R\)).

entries.title: Derived Limit
entries.body: \(\varprojlim^1 A_i\) denotes the first right-derived functor of \(\varprojlim\), measuring failure of right exactness.

entries.title: Compact Object
entries.body: An object \(C\) is **compact** if\(\operatorname{Hom}(C,-)\) commutes with arbitrary filtered colimits.

entries.title: Exact Couple
entries.body:
An **exact couple** is a diagram
\[D\xrightarrow{i}D\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{k}D\]
with exactness at each vertex in the repeating sequence
\[\cdots\to D\xrightarrow{i}D\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{k}D\xrightarrow{i}D\cdots\].

entries.title: Spectral Sequence
entries.body:
A **spectral sequence** is a collection \((E_r^{p,q},d_r)\) for \(r\ge2\), where each
\(d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}\), and 
\(E_{r+1}^{p,q}\cong H(E_r^{p,q},d_r)\).

entries.title: Filtration
entries.body:
A **filtration** of object \(A\) is a chain
\(\cdots\subseteq F^{p+1}A\subseteq F^pA\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A\).

entries.title: Associated Graded Object
entries.body:
Given filtration \(F^\bullet A\), the associated graded object is
\(\mathrm{Gr}^pA=F^pA/F^{p+1}A\).

entries.title: Spectral Sequence Convergence
entries.body:
A spectral sequence \((E_r,d_r)\) **converges** to \(H\) if it stabilizes on pages
\(E_\infty\) and reproduces a filtered object with associated graded isomorphic to \(E_\infty\).

entries.title: Triangulated Category
entries.body:
A **triangulated category** is an additive category with shift functor \([1]\) and distinguished triangles
\(X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]\), satisfying Verdier axioms.

entries.title: t-Structure
entries.body:
A **t-structure** on a triangulated category \(\mathcal D\) is a pair \((\mathcal D^{\le 0},\mathcal D^{\ge 0})\) such that
\(\mathcal D^{\le 0}\subseteq\mathcal D^{\le 1}\), \(\mathcal D^{\ge 0}\supseteq\mathcal D^{\ge 1}\), and every object fits into a triangle with truncations.

entries.title: Heart of a t-Structure
entries.body: The **heart** is \(\mathcal A=\mathcal D^{\le 0}\cap\mathcal D^{\ge 0}\), which is an abelian category.

entries.title: Long Exact Cohomology Sequence
entries.body:
For a distinguished triangle \(X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]\), there is a long exact sequence
\(\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(Y)\to H^n(Z)\to H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots\).

entries.title: Compact Generation
entries.body: A triangulated category is **compactly generated** if a set of compact objects detects zero objects via\(\mathrm{Hom}(C, -)=0\).

entries.title: Thick Subcategory
entries.body: A full triangulated subcategory \(\mathcal T\subset\mathcal D\) is **thick** if closed under direct summands and distinguished triangles.

entries.title: Verdier Quotient
entries.body: For triangulated \(\mathcal D\) and thick subcategory \(\mathcal T\), the Verdier quotient \(\mathcal D/\mathcal T\) formally inverts morphisms whose cone lies in \(\mathcal T\).

entries.title: Bousfield Localization
entries.body: A **Bousfield localization** is an exact functor \(L:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\) with natural map \(\eta: \mathrm{Id}\to L\), such that \(L\eta\) and \(\eta L\) are isomorphisms and \(L\eta_X\) is initial among maps to \(L\)-local objects.

entries.title: Brown Representability
entries.body: A triangulated category satisfies **Brown representability** if every cohomological functor that converts coproducts to products is representable.

entries.title: Derived Equivalence
entries.body:
Two rings/category \(A,B\) are **derived equivalent** if
\(D(A)\simeq D(B)\), often through a tilting complex or Fourier--Mukai-style transform.

entries.title: Grothendieck Category
entries.body: An abelian category \(\mathcal A\) is a **Grothendieck category** if it has exact filtered colimits, a generator, and arbitrary coproducts.

entries.title: Compact Object
entries.body:
An object \(C\) is **compact** if
\[
\mathrm{Hom}(C,\bigoplus_i X_i)\cong\bigoplus_i\mathrm{Hom}(C,X_i).
\]

entries.title: Tensor Category
entries.body: A **tensor category** is a category \((\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf1)\) with a bifunctor \(\otimes\) and associativity/unit constraints.

entries.title: Quillen Adjunction
entries.body: A pair \(L\dashv R\) is a **Quillen adjunction** if \(L\) preserves cofibrations and \(R\) preserves fibrations.

entries.title: Abelianization
entries.body: For a group \(G\), the **abelianization** is \(G^{ab}=G/[G,G]\), the universal abelian quotient.

entries.title: Monoidal Category
entries.body: A **monoidal category** has a tensor product \(\otimes\), unit object \(\mathbf 1\), and coherent associativity constraints.

entries.title: Tannakian Category
entries.body: For a field \(k\), a **Tannakian category** is a rigid symmetric monoidal \(k\)-linear category with a faithful exact fiber functor.

entries.title: Koszul Complex
entries.body: Given \(R\)-sequence \(x_1,\dots,x_n\), the **Koszul complex** \(K_\bullet(x_1,\dots,x_n)\) computes algebraic dependence of the sequence.

entries.title: Ext Functor
entries.body: For modules \(M,N\), \(\mathrm{Ext}^n_R(M,N)\) is the right-derived functor of \(\mathrm{Hom}_R(M,-)\), classifying \(n\)-fold extensions.

entries.title: Morita Equivalence
entries.body: Rings \(A\) and \(B\) are **Morita equivalent** if \(A\)-Mod and \(B\)-Mod are equivalent categories.

entries.title: Degree Measure
entries.body: One full turn equals \(360^\circ\).

entries.title: Radian
entries.body: One radian is arc length divided by radius; full turn is \(2\pi\) radians.

entries.title: Steradian
entries.body: A **steradian** is a unit of solid angle in 3D; the full sphere subtends \(4\pi\) steradians.

entries.title: Reference Angle
entries.body: Smallest nonnegative angle from terminal side to x-axis.

entries.title: Coterminal Angles
entries.body: Angles \(\theta\) and \(\theta+2k\pi\) have same terminal side for integer \(k\).

entries.title: Sine
entries.body: \(\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\).

entries.title: Cosine
entries.body: \(\cos\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\).

entries.title: Tangent
entries.body: \(\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\).

entries.title: Secant
entries.body: \(\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\).

entries.title: Cosecant
entries.body: \(\csc\theta=\frac{1}{\sin\theta}\).

entries.title: Cotangent
entries.body: \(\cot\theta=\frac{1}{\tan\theta}=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\).

entries.title: Unit Circle
entries.body: Set of points \((x,y)\) satisfying \(x^2+y^2=1\).

entries.title: Sine-Cosine Pair
entries.body: For angle \(\theta\), coordinates are \((\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\).

entries.title: Quadrant Sign Rule
entries.body: In each quadrant, signs of \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\), \(\tan\theta\) are determined by \(x,y\) signs.

entries.title: Special Angles
entries.body: Common exact values use \(\{30^\circ,45^\circ,60^\circ\}\).

entries.title: Pythagorean Identity
entries.body: \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\).

entries.title: Reciprocal Pythagorean Identity
entries.body: \(1+\cot^2\theta=\csc^2\theta\).

entries.title: Angle Addition Formula
entries.body: \(\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta\).

entries.title: Double-Angle Formula
entries.body: \(\sin(2\theta)=2\sin\theta\cos\theta\).

entries.title: Product-to-Sum Identity
entries.body: \(\sin\alpha\sin\beta=\frac12[\cos(\alpha-\beta)-\cos(\alpha+\beta)]\).

entries.title: Period
entries.body: \(f(x+T)=f(x)\) for minimal \(T>0\).

entries.title: Phase Shift
entries.body: \(\sin(x-\phi)\) shifts graph right by \(\phi\).

entries.title: Amplitude
entries.body: For \(A\sin x\), amplitude is \(|A|\).

entries.title: Midline
entries.body: Midline of \(A\sin x+B\) is the horizontal line \(y=B\).

entries.title: Arcsine
entries.body: \(\arcsin x\) gives \(\theta\) with \(\sin\theta=x\).

entries.title: Arccosine
entries.body: \(\arccos x\) gives \(\theta\) with \(\cos\theta=x\).

entries.title: Arctangent Principal Value
entries.body: \(\arctan x\) takes values in \((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\).

entries.title: Atan2 Function
entries.body: \(\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)\) gives angle accounting for quadrant of \((x,y)\).

entries.title: Law of Sines
entries.body: For triangle \(ABC\), \(\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}\).

entries.title: Area by Sines
entries.body: Triangle area: \(\frac12 ab\sin C\).

entries.title: Basic Trigonometric Equation
entries.body: \(\sin x = k\) has two principal reference-angle families before periodic extension.

entries.title: Harmonic Motion Equation
entries.body: Standard form: \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\).

entries.title: Pythagorean Identity
entries.body:
For all real \(\theta\),
\[
\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1.
\]

entries.title: Angle Sum Formula
entries.body:
For all real \(\alpha,\beta\),
\[
\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta,
\]
\[
\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta-\sin\alpha\sin\beta.
\]

entries.title: Law of Sines
entries.body:
For triangle \(ABC\),
\[
\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}=2R,
\]
where \(R\) is circumradius.

entries.title: Periodicity of Sine and Cosine
entries.body: \(\sin(\theta+2\pi)=\sin\theta\), \(\cos(\theta+2\pi)=\cos\theta\).

entries.title: Special Angle Evaluation
entries.body:
\[
\sin 30^\circ=\frac12,\quad \cos 60^\circ=\frac12,\quad \tan 45^\circ=1.
\]

entries.title: Use of Angle Addition
entries.body:
\[
\sin 75^\circ=\sin(45^\circ+30^\circ)=\frac{\sqrt 2}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.
\]

entries.title: Solve a Trig Equation
entries.body:
Solve \(\sin x=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\):
\[
x=\frac{\pi}{4}+2k\pi\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{3\pi}{4}+2k\pi,\quad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]

entries.title: Q1. Evaluate \(\sin 75^\circ\) exactly.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Use addition with \(75^\circ=45^\circ+30^\circ\):
\[
\sin75^\circ=\sin(45^\circ+30^\circ)
=\sin45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\cos45^\circ\sin30^\circ
\]
\[
=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac12
=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.
\]

entries.title: Q2. Solve \(\sin x=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\) for real \(x\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** First principal solutions in \([0,2\pi)\) are \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\) and \(x=\frac{3\pi}{4}\) in quadrant I and II.
Periodicity gives period \(2\pi\), so the full solution set is
\[
x=\frac{\pi}{4}+2k\pi\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{3\pi}{4}+2k\pi,\quad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]

entries.title: Q3. Prove the periodicity of sine: \(\sin(\theta+2\pi)=\sin\theta\).
entries.body: **Answer.** On the unit circle, angles differing by \(2\pi\) have the same terminal point because one full revolution returns to the same point. Therefore both coordinates are equal, including the y-coordinate, so \(\sin(\theta+2\pi)=\sin\theta\). The same argument gives \(\cos(\theta+2\pi)=\cos\theta\).

entries.title: Q4. Verify \(\arcsin\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\).
entries.body: **Answer.** Since by definition \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\), and \(\arcsin\) returns the unique value in \([-\pi/2,\pi/2]\) with the given sine, the answer follows.

entries.title: Q5. Prove \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) when \(\cos\theta\neq 0\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** By definition in right-triangle interpretation, \(\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\) and \(\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\).
When \(\cos\theta\neq 0\), adjacent \(\neq 0\). Then
\[
\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=
\frac{\text{opp}/\text{hyp}}{\text{adj}/\text{hyp}}=
\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\tan\theta.
\]

entries.title: Q6. Derive \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) from unit circle coordinates.
entries.body:
**Answer.** A point on unit circle at angle \(\theta\) is \((\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\). It satisfies
\[
\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1^2=1,
\]
because radius is 1.

entries.title: Q7. Solve \(\cos x =0\) on \([0,2\pi)\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** \(\cos x=0\) at angles whose terminal point has x-coordinate 0:
\[
x=\frac{\pi}{2},\;\frac{3\pi}{2}.
\]
These are the only solutions in the interval.

entries.title: Q8. Prove \(\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** On the unit circle, angle \(-\theta\) reflects \((\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\) across the x-axis, which changes y-coordinate sign and leaves x-coordinate unchanged.
Hence \(\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta\) (even) and \(\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta\) (odd).

entries.title: Law of Cosines
entries.body:
For a triangle with side lengths \(a,b,c\) opposite corresponding angles \(A,B,C\):
\[
 c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C,
\]
and cyclic permutations hold.

entries.title: Sine Law
entries.body:
For a triangle \(ABC\) with inradius \(R\) (circumradius),
\[
\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}=2R,
\]
where \(a,b,c\) are opposite sides.

entries.title: Half-Angle Formula Set
entries.body:
For \(\theta\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{2},\qquad
\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}.
\]

entries.title: Inverse Sine Principal Value Existence and Uniqueness
entries.body:
There is a unique function \(\arcsin:(-1,1)\to\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) such that
\[
\sin(\arcsin x)=x\quad(\forall x\in[-1,1]).
\]

entries.title: Sum-to-Product
entries.body:
For all real \(x,y\),
\[
\sin x+\sin y=2\sin\frac{x+y}{2}\cos\frac{x-y}{2},\qquad
\cos x+\cos y=2\cos\frac{x+y}{2}\cos\frac{x-y}{2}.
\]

entries.title: Q1. Law of Cosines (Proof idea)
entries.body:
In triangle with sides \(a,b,c\), drop altitude from vertex of angle \(C\) to side \(c\): split into right triangle pieces of lengths \(b\cos C\) and \(b\sin C\). Then remaining segment on side \(c\) is \(a-b\cos C\).
By Pythagoras:
\[
 c^2 = (a-b\cos C)^2 + (b\sin C)^2 = a^2 + b^2 -2ab\cos C.
\]
This is exactly the law.

entries.title: Q2. Sine Law (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Use triangle area in two ways:
\[
[\triangle ABC]=\frac12 ab\sin C = \frac12 bc\sin A=\frac12 ca\sin B.
\]
So dividing by \(\frac12 abc\) (all sides nonzero),
\[
\frac{\sin A}{a}=\frac{\sin B}{b}=\frac{\sin C}{c}=\frac{1}{2R}.
\]
Hence \(\frac{a}{\sin A}=2R\) and cyclic.

entries.title: Q3. Half-angle identity (Proof idea)
entries.body:
From double-angle:
\[
\cos\theta = 1-2\sin^2\frac\theta2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \sin^2\frac\theta2 = \frac{1-\cos\theta}{2}.
\]
Also
\[
\cos\theta = 2\cos^2\frac\theta2 -1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \cos^2\frac\theta2 = \frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}.
\]
Take square roots with sign determined by \(\theta/2\)'s quadrant when needed.

entries.title: Q4. Inverse Sine Principal Value (Proof idea)
entries.body: Restrict \(x\in[-1,1]\). Function \(\sin\) on \([-\pi/2,\pi/2]\) is continuous and strictly increasing from \(-1\) to \(1\), therefore bijective onto \([-1,1]\). By inverse function theorem on monotone continuous maps, a unique inverse function exists there, denoted \(\arcsin\), with \(\sin(\arcsin x)=x\).

entries.title: Q5. Sum-to-Product (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Use addition formulas:
\[
\sin x+\sin y=\sin\left(\frac{x+y}{2}+\frac{x-y}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{x+y}{2}-\frac{x-y}{2}\right).
\]
Applying \(\sin(u\pm v)=\sin u\cos v\pm\cos u\sin v\), terms combine to
\[
=2\sin\frac{x+y}{2}\cos\frac{x-y}{2}.
\]
Similarly for cosines,
\[
\cos x+\cos y=2\cos\frac{x+y}{2}\cos\frac{x-y}{2}.
\]

entries.title: Euler Formula
entries.body:
the identity \\(
e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta\\), linking complex exponentials with trigonometric functions.

entries.title: Hyperbolic Sine

a function defined by \\(

\\)

the function \\(
\operatorname{arctan} x=\tan^{-1}x
\\), the principal inverse of \\(\tan\\) on \\((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\\).

a trig identity relating complementary angles, e.g. \\(
\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)=\cos\theta.
\\)

entries.title: Phase
entries.body:
the constant \\(\phi\
\) in \\(
a\sin(bx+\phi)\) describing horizontal shift of a sinusoid.

entries.title: Hyperbolic Cosine
entries.body:
a hyperbolic function defined by \(
\cosh x=\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}{2}.
\)

entries.title: Hyperbolic Tangent
entries.body:
the ratio \(
\tanh x=\frac{\sinh x}{\cosh x}=\frac{e^{2x}-1}{e^{2x}+1}.
\)

entries.title: Inverse Cotangent
entries.body: a function \(\operatorname{arccot} x\) satisfying \(\cot(\operatorname{arccot}x)=x\) on its principal branch.

entries.title: Trigonometric Polynomial
entries.body:
a finite linear combination
\[
\sum_{k=0}^n a_k\cos(kx)+b_k\sin(kx).
\]

entries.title: Lissajous Curve
entries.body:
a parametric curve
\[
(x,y)=(A\sin(at+\delta),B\sin(bt))
\]
with frequency ratio \(a\!:\!b\).

Inverse Hyperbolic Sine
entries.body:
\[
\operatorname{arcsinh}x=\ln\!\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)
\]
for \(x\in\mathbb R\).

entries.body:

\]

entries.body:

\]

\operatorname{sinc}x=
\begin{cases}
\frac{\sin x}{x},&x\ne0,\\
1,&x=0.
