\]

entries.title: Euler's Formula
entries.body:
For real or complex 


$z$,


\(e^{iz}=\cos z+i\sin z\).

entries.title: Complex Sine
entries.body:
For 


$z\in\mathbb C$,


\(\sin z=\dfrac{e^{iz}-e^{-iz}}{2i}\).

entries.title: Complex Cosine
entries.body:
For 


$z\in\mathbb C$,


\(\cos z=\dfrac{e^{iz}+e^{-iz}}2\).

entries.title: Hyperbolic Sine
entries.body:
The **hyperbolic sine** is 


\(\sinh x=\dfrac{e^x-e^{-x}}2\).

entries.title: Hyperbolic Cosine
entries.body:
The **hyperbolic cosine** is 


\(\cosh x=\dfrac{e^x+e^{-x}}2\), so that 


\(\cosh^2x-\sinh^2x=1\).

entries.title: Phasor Representation
entries.body:
A sinusoid 


$A\cos(\omega t+\phi)$


is represented by complex form 


$Ae^{i\phi}e^{i\omega t}$,


whose real part recovers the original wave.

entries.title: Trigonometric Substitution
entries.body:
For integrals with 


$\sqrt{a^2-x^2}$,


set 


$x=a\sin\theta$.

For 


$a^2+x^2$,


set 


$x=a\tan\theta$.

entries.title: Rotation Matrix
entries.body:
The 2D rotation by angle 


$\theta$ has matrix


\[


R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.

\]

entries.title: Fourier Coefficients
entries.body:
A 2\pi-periodic function has coefficients


\[

a_n=\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos(nx)\,dx,


b_n=\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\sin(nx)\,dx.

\]

entries.title: Trigonometric Polynomial
entries.body:
A finite sum


\[
\sum_{k=-N}^N c_k e^{ikx}=


 a_0+\sum_{k=1}^N(a_k\cos kx+b_k\sin kx)

\]
is a 


**trigonometric polynomial**.

entries.title: Inverse Secant
entries.body:
the function 


$\operatorname{sec}^{-1}x=\arccos(1/x)$


with principal values in 


$[0,\pi]\setminus\{\pi/2\}$.

entries.title: Inverse Cosecant
entries.body:
The 


$\operatorname{csc}^{-1}x=\arcsin(1/x)$


has principal values in 


$[-\pi/2,\pi/2]\setminus\{0\}$.

entries.title: Parametric Form of Circle
entries.body:
A circle of radius 


$r$ is parametrized by


\[(x(t),y(t))=(r\cos t,r\sin t).\]

entries.title: Trigonometric Parametric Differentiation
entries.body:
For parametric curves 


$x=x(t), y=y(t)$,


derivatives satisfy


\[\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{dy}{dt}}{\frac{dx}{dt}}\]


when 


$\frac{dx}{dt}\neq0$.

entries.title: Arctangent Identity for Two Variables
entries.body:
For 


$x\neq0$, 


\[
\arctan x+\arctan y=\arctan\frac{x+y}{1-xy}


\]


with quadrant adjustment as needed.

entries.title: Triple-Angle Formula
entries.body:
\[
\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta-4\sin^3\theta,
\qquad
\cos 3\theta=4\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta.
\]

entries.title: Product-to-Sum (Cross)
entries.body:
\[
\sin\alpha\cos\beta=\frac12[\sin(\alpha+\beta)+\sin(\alpha-\beta)].
\]

entries.title: Sum-to-Product (Cross)
entries.body:
\[
\sin\alpha+\sin\beta=2\sin\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}.
\]

entries.title: Trigonometric Substitution via Tangent Half-Angle
entries.body:
Set 


$t=\tan(\theta/2)$


to rewrite trig expressions as rational functions via


\[
\sin\theta=\frac{2t}{1+t^2},\quad
\cos\theta=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2},\quad
\mathrm d\theta=\frac{2}{1+t^2}\,\mathrm dt.
\]

entries.title: Wave Equation Solution Form
entries.body:
For 


$u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$,


the d'Alembert form is


\[u(x,t)=F(x-ct)+G(x+ct).\]

entries.title: Fejér Kernel
entries.body:
The **Fejér kernel** is
\[
F_n(t)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^{n}D_k(t)=\frac1{n+1}\left(\frac{\sin\frac{(n+1)t}{2}}{\sin\frac t2}\right)^2.
\]

entries.title: Dirichlet Kernel
entries.body:
The **Dirichlet kernel** is
\[
D_n(t)=\sum_{k=-n}^n e^{ikt}=1+2\sum_{k=1}^n\cos(kt)=\frac{\sin((n+\tfrac12)t)}{\sin(t/2)}.
\]

entries.title: Fourier Series Convergence (Dirichlet)
entries.body:
If \(f\) is piecewise \(C^1\), its Fourier series converges to 
\((f(x^+)+f(x^-))/2\) at each point.

entries.title: Parseval Identity
entries.body:
For square-summable coefficients \(a_n,b_n\),
\[
\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)^2\,dx=\frac{a_0^2}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n^2+b_n^2).
\]

entries.title: Gibbs Phenomenon
entries.body: Near jump discontinuities, Fourier partial sums overshoot by approximately 9%, and oscillatory overshoot does not vanish as truncation order grows.

entries.title: Hilbert Transform
entries.body:
The **Hilbert transform** of \(f\) is
\[
\mathcal H f(x)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{f(t)}{x-t}\,dt.
\]

entries.title: Convolution with Kernel
entries.body:
If \((k\ast f)(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}k(x-t)f(t)\,dt\),
then many trig filters are realized as convolutions.

entries.title: Fractional Fourier Transform
entries.body: The **fractional Fourier transform** \(\mathcal F_\alpha\) generalizes \(\mathcal F\) by rotating in the time-frequency plane by angle \(\alpha\).

entries.title: Angular Frequency
entries.body: Angular frequency is \(\omega=2\pi f\), where \(f\) is linear frequency.

entries.title: Phase Modulation
entries.body:
A **phase modulation** signal has form
\[
A\cos(\omega t+\phi(t)).
\]
If \(\phi'\equiv c\), this is a shifted pure tone.

entries.title: Fourier Series
entries.body:
A periodic function can be written as
\[
 f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^\infty(a_n\cos nx+b_n\sin nx),
\]
where \(a_n\) and \(b_n\) are Fourier coefficients.

entries.title: Dirichlet Kernel
entries.body: \(D_n(x)=\sum_{k=-n}^{n}e^{ikx}=1+2\sum_{k=1}^{n}\cos(kx)\), used in trigonometric partial sums.

entries.title: Parseval Identity
entries.body:
For orthogonal trig basis,
\[
\frac1{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|f(x)|^2dx=\frac{a_0^2}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n^2+b_n^2).
\]

entries.title: Angular Frequency
entries.body: If the period is \(T\), angular frequency is \(\omega=\frac{2\pi}{T}\), so waves are \(A\cos(\omega x+\phi)\).

entries.title: Harmonic Mean Value
entries.body:
For a pure tone represented as sine-cosine pair, the combined phase satisfies
\(A\cos(\omega x)+B\sin(\omega x)=R\cos(\omega x-\delta)\), with \(R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\).

entries.title: Euler's Formula
entries.body:
For real \(x\),
\[
\exp(ix)=\cos x+i\sin x.
\]

entries.title: Exponential to Trig Conversions
entries.body:
\[
\sin x=\frac{e^{ix}-e^{-ix}}{2i},\quad
\cos x=\frac{e^{ix}+e^{-ix}}{2}.
\]

entries.title: De Moivre's Identity
entries.body:
For integer \(n\),
\[
\left(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta\right)^n=\cos(n\theta)+i\sin(n\theta).
\]

entries.title: Nth Roots of Unity
entries.body:
Solutions of \(z^n=1\) are
\[
z_k=e^{2\pi ik/n}=\cos\frac{2\pi k}{n}+i\sin\frac{2\pi k}{n},\;k=0,\dots,n-1.
\]

entries.title: Chebyshev Relation
entries.body:
The Chebyshev polynomial satisfies
\[
\cos(n\theta)=T_n(\cos\theta).
\]

entries.title: Orthogonality of Sine-Cosine Basis
entries.body:
On \([-\pi,\pi]\),
\[
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\sin(nx)\sin(mx)\,dx=\begin{cases}0,&n\ne m,\\ \,\pi,&n=m\ne0,\end{cases}
\]
and similarly for cosine terms with mixed products integrating to zero.

entries.title: Parseval-Plancherel for Fourier Series
entries.body:
For square-integrable periodic \(f\),
\[
\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|f(x)|^2dx=\frac{a_0^2}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n^2+b_n^2).
\]

entries.title: Gibbs Phenomenon
entries.body: A Fourier partial sum near a jump discontinuity overshoots by about 9% of jump size and converges with oscillations.

entries.title: Cesàro Summation
entries.body: A divergent oscillatory trigonometric series may be assigned a summed value by averaging partial sums (Fejér means).

entries.title: Dirichlet Kernel Norm
entries.body: The \(L^1\)-norm \(\|D_n\|_1\) grows like \(O(\log n)\), underpinning poor pointwise behavior of pointwise Fourier sums.

entries.title: Dirichlet Kernel
entries.body:
The Dirichlet kernel is
\[
D_n(\theta)=1+2\sum_{k=1}^n\cos(k\theta)=\frac{\sin\left((n+\tfrac12)\theta\right)}{\sin(\theta/2)}.
\]

entries.title: Fejér Kernel
entries.body:
Fejér kernel is
\[
F_n(\theta)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{m=0}^{n}D_m(\theta)=\frac1{n+1}\left(\frac{\sin\frac{(n+1)\theta}{2}}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}\right)^2.
\]

entries.title: Spherical Harmonic Link
entries.body:
On the unit sphere, trig terms generalize to
\(Y_{\ell}^m(\theta,\phi)=N\,P_{\ell}^m(\cos\theta)e^{im\phi}\).

entries.title: Poisson Kernel
entries.body:
For \(|r|<1\),
\[
P_r(\theta)=1+2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}r^n\cos(n\theta)=\frac{1-r^2}{1-2r\cos\theta+r^2}.
\]

entries.title: Trigonometric Polynomial
entries.body:
A **trigonometric polynomial** is
\[
T(\theta)=a_0+\sum_{k=1}^n(a_k\cos k\theta+b_k\sin k\theta).
\]

entries.title: Poisson Summation Formula
entries.body:
For suitable \(f\),
\[
\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}f(k)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\hat f(n),\qquad
\hat f(\xi)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}f(x)e^{-2\pi i\xi x}\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Jacobi-Anger Expansion
entries.body:
\[
\exp\big(i z\cos\theta\big)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}i^n J_n(z)e^{in\theta},
\]
where \(J_n\) are Bessel functions.

entries.title: Spherical Trigonometric Form
entries.body: A zonal harmonic expansion uses terms\(P_n(\cos\theta)\), while circular harmonics use \(\cos(n\theta),\sin(n\theta)\) as the 1D basis.

entries.title: Gibbs Constant
entries.body:
Near jump points, partial Fourier sums approach overshoot of approximately \\(rac{\text{jump}}{\pi^2}\sum_{k=1}^
fty\frac{\sin(k\theta)}{k}\) with limiting envelope known as Gibbs constant.

entries.title: Cesàro-Convergence of Fourier Series
entries.body: If ordinary partial sums fail pointwise, Cesàro means\(\sigma_n f\) still converge at regular points to \((f(x^+)+f(x^-))/2\).

entries.title: Circular Convolution
entries.body:
For\(2\pi\)-periodic functions,
\[
(f\ast g)(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x-t)g(t)\,dt.
\]

entries.title: Dirichlet Convolution of Coefficients
entries.body:
For arithmetic-like trig sequences, convolution of coefficient sequences is
\[(a\ast b)_n=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kb_{n-k}.\]

entries.title: Fejér Mean
entries.body:
The \(n\)-th Fejér mean is
\[
\sigma_n(x)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^n S_k(x),
\]
where \(S_k\) is the \(k\)-th partial Fourier sum.

entries.title: Bochner Integrable Periodic Function
entries.body:
A function on \([-\pi,\pi]\) is Bochner integrable if it is measurable and
\(\int\|f(x)|dx<\infty\); its Fourier coefficients are well-defined and finite.

entries.title: Band-Limited Representation
entries.body: A trigonometric series with \(a_n=b_n=0\) for \(|n|>N\) is **band-limited** to frequency \(N\).

entries.title: Asymptotic Expansion of Oscillatory Integrals
entries.body:
For smooth \(\phi\) with nondegenerate stationary point \(x_0\),
\[
\int e^{i\lambda\phi(x)}a(x)dx\sim e^{i\lambda\phi(x_0)}\sum_{k\ge0}c_k\lambda^{-k-1/2},\quad \lambda\to\infty.
\]

entries.title: Sine Integral
entries.body:
\[
\operatorname{Si}(x)=\int_0^x\frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt.
\]

entries.title: Cosine Integral
entries.body:
\[
\operatorname{Ci}(x)=-\int_x^\infty \frac{\cos t}{t}\,dt.
\]

entries.title: Dirac Comb
entries.body:
The Dirac comb is
\(\Sha_T(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\delta(x-kT)\), connecting periodicity and Fourier sampling.

entries.title: Distributional Trigonometric Identity
entries.body:
In distribution sense,
\[\sin(ax)\delta(x-b)=\sin(ab)\delta(x-b),\qquad
\cos(ax)\delta(x-b)=\cos(ab)\delta(x-b).\]

entries.title: Hilbert Transform
entries.body:
The Hilbert transform of \(f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is
\[
\mathcal Hf(t)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{f(\tau)}{t-\tau}\,d\tau,
\]
shifting phase by \(\pm \pi/2\).

entries.title: Analytic Signal
entries.body:
For real signal \(x(t)\), analytic signal is
\(z(t)=x(t)+i\mathcal Hx(t)\), with instantaneous amplitude \(|z(t)|\).

entries.title: Fractional Period Shift
entries.body:
If \(f(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\), then 
\(\mathcal F_\alpha\{f\}\) corresponds to phase scaling by exponent matrix with fractional power \(\alpha\) (in fractional Fourier analysis).

entries.title: Harmonic Addition Formula
entries.body:
For coefficients \(a_n,b_n\):
\[
\sin\alpha\pm\sin\beta=2\sin\frac{\alpha\pm\beta}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha\mp\beta}{2},
\]
\[
\cos\alpha\pm\cos\beta=2\cos\frac{\alpha\pm\beta}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha\mp\beta}{2}.
\]

entries.title: Windowed Fourier Coefficient
entries.body:
For window \(w\), short-time Fourier coefficient is
\[
V_w f(t,\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}f(x)\overline{w(x-t)}e^{-2\pi i\omega x}\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Dirichlet Kernel
entries.body:
The **Dirichlet kernel** is
\[
D_n(\theta)=1+2\sum_{k=1}^n\cos(k\theta)=\frac{\sin\left(n+\frac12\right)\theta}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}.
\]

entries.title: Fejér Kernel
entries.body:
The **Fejér kernel** is the arithmetic mean of Dirichlet kernels:
\[
F_n(\theta)=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^n D_k(\theta)=\frac{1}{n+1}\left(\frac{\sin\frac{n+1}{2}\theta}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}\right)^2.
\]

entries.title: Jacobi-Anger Expansion
entries.body:
For \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
e^{iz\sin\theta}=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}J_m(z)e^{im\theta},
\]
with Bessel functions \(J_m\).

entries.title: Bessel Function of the First Kind
entries.body:
The order-\(n\) Bessel function can be written as
\[
J_n(x)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^\pi \cos(n\tau-x\sin\tau)\,d\tau.
\]

entries.title: Chebyshev Polynomial
entries.body:
For \(x=\cos\theta\),
\[
T_n(x)=\cos(n\theta).
\]

entries.title: Trigonometric Polynomial
entries.body:
A finite sum
\[
\sum_{k=-N}^N c_k e^{ikx}
\]
is a **trigonometric polynomial**.

entries.title: Dirichlet Convergence Theorem
entries.body: If \(f\in L^1[-\pi,\pi]\), then Fourier partial sums \(S_Nf(x)\) converge to \(\frac{f(x^+)+f(x^-)}2\) at jump points.

entries.title: Parseval Identity
entries.body:
For \(f\in L^2[-\pi,\pi]\), Fourier coefficients \(c_n\) satisfy
\[
\frac1{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|f(x)|^2\,dx
=2\sum_{n=1}^\infty|c_n|^2+|c_0|^2.
\]

entries.title: Riemann--Lebesgue Lemma
entries.body:
For \(f\in L^1[-\pi,\pi]\), Fourier coefficients satisfy
\[
\hat f(n)\to0\quad \text{as }|n|\to\infty.
\]

entries.title: Gibbs Phenomenon
entries.body: Near a jump discontinuity, Fourier partial sums overshoot by about \(9\%\) and do not converge uniformly to the midpoint profile.

entries.title: Limit
entries.body: \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L\).

entries.title: Epsilon-Delta Definition
entries.body: \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L\) if for all \(\epsilon>0\), exists \(\delta>0\) with \(0<|x-a|<\delta \Rightarrow |f(x)-L|<\epsilon\).

entries.title: Continuity at a Point
entries.body: \(f\) continuous at \(a\) if \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a)\).

entries.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
entries.body: If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and \(y\) lies between \(f(a),f(b)\), then \(\exists c\in(a,b):f(c)=y\).

entries.title: Types of Discontinuity
entries.body: Removable, jump, and infinite discontinuities classify non-continuity points.

entries.title: Derivative
entries.body: \(f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\).

entries.title: Quotient Rule
entries.body: \(\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)'=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}\).

entries.title: Hessian (second derivative matrix)
entries.body: \(H_{ij}=\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}\).

entries.title: Critical Point
entries.body: \(x=a\) with \(f'(a)=0\) or undefined.

entries.title: Monotonicity
entries.body: If \(f'(x)>0\), \(f\) increases on interval.

entries.title: Fermat's Theorem
entries.body: If \(f\) has local extremum at interior \(a\) and is differentiable there, then \(f'(a)=0\).

entries.title: Concavity
entries.body: \(f''(x)>0\): concave up; \(f''(x)<0\): concave down.

entries.title: Inflection Point
entries.body: Point where concavity changes sign.

entries.title: Differential Approximation
entries.body: \(f(x+h)\approx f(x)+f'(x)h\).

entries.title: Mean Value Theorem
entries.body: Exists \(c\in(a,b)\) with \(f'(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}\).

entries.title: Indefinite Integral
entries.body: \(\int f(x)\,dx\).

entries.title: Constant of Integration
entries.body: Any antiderivative differs by additive constant \(C\).

entries.title: Definite Integral
entries.body: \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\).

entries.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
entries.body: \(\frac{d}{dx}\int_a^x f(t)dt = f(x)\).

entries.title: Substitution
entries.body: Replace \(u=g(x)\) to simplify integrals.

entries.title: Integration by Parts
entries.body: \(\int u\,dv = uv-\int v\,du\).

entries.title: Trig Substitution
entries.body: Substitute \(\sin\), \(\cos\), or \(\tan\) for \(\sqrt{a^2-x^2}\)-style forms.

entries.title: Improper Integral
entries.body: Integral where limits or integrand are unbounded.

entries.title: Convergent Sequence
entries.body: \(a_n\to L\).

entries.title: Cauchy Sequence
entries.body: Sequence with \(\forall\epsilon>0\,\exists N:\forall m,n\ge N,\ |a_n-a_m|<\epsilon\).

entries.title: Comparison Test
entries.body: If \(0\le a_n\le b_n\) and \(\sum b_n\) converges, then \(\sum a_n\) converges.

entries.title: Ratio Test
entries.body: If \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right|=L\): converges for \(L<1\), diverges for \(L>1\).

entries.title: Power Series
entries.body: \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n(x-a)^n\).

entries.title: Radius of Convergence
entries.body: Set of \(x\) where series converges, centered at \(a\), with radius \(R\).

entries.title: Partial Derivative
entries.body: \(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\).

entries.title: Mixed Partial Derivative
entries.body: \(\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x\partial y}\).

entries.title: Double Integral
entries.body: \(\iint_R f(x,y)\,dA\) accumulates over regions in the plane.

entries.title: Polar Double Integral
entries.body: \(\iint_R f(r,\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta\).

entries.title: Separable ODE
entries.body: \(\frac{dy}{dx}=g(x)h(y)\) can be separated.

entries.title: Exact Equation
entries.body: \(M(x,y)+N(x,y)\) with \(M_y=N_x\) gives \(\partial F/\partial x=M,\partial F/\partial y=N\).

entries.title: Linear First-Order ODE
entries.body: \(\frac{dy}{dx}+P(x)y=Q(x)\).

entries.title: Integrating Factor
entries.body: \(\mu(x)=e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) multiplies linear first-order ODE.

entries.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part I
entries.body:
If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\), then
\[
\frac{d}{dx}\left(\int_a^x f(t)\,dt\right)=f(x),\quad x\in(a,b).
\]

entries.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part II
entries.body:
If \(f\) is continuous and \(F\) is any antiderivative, then
\[
\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=F(b)-F(a).
\]

entries.title: Mean Value Theorem
entries.body:
If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and differentiable on \((a,b)\), there exists \(c\in(a,b)\) such that
\[
f'(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
\]

entries.title: Integration by Parts
entries.body:
For differentiable \(u,v\):
\[
\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du.
\]

entries.title: Solve ODE by Separation
entries.body:
For \(\frac{dy}{dx}=3y\), separate: \(\frac{1}{y}dy=3dx\).
Integrating:
\[
\ln|y|=3x+C\Rightarrow y=Ce^{3x}.
\]

entries.title: Q1. Differentiate \(f(x)=x^4-2x^2+3x-1\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Apply the power rule to each term:
\[
\frac{d}{dx}(x^4)=4x^3,
\quad
\frac{d}{dx}(-2x^2)=-4x,
\quad
\frac{d}{dx}(3x)=3,
\quad
\frac{d}{dx}(-1)=0.
\]
So
\[
f'(x)=4x^3-4x+3.
\]

entries.title: Q2. Compute \(\int_0^1 (3x^2+2x)\,dx\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Find an antiderivative:
\[
\int(3x^2+2x)dx=x^3+x^2+C.
\]
Apply FTC:
\[
\int_0^1(3x^2+2x)dx=[x^3+x^2]_0^1=(1+1)-0=2.
\]

entries.title: Q3. Apply the Mean Value Theorem to \(f(x)=x^2\) on \([1,3]\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** \(f\) is continuous on \([1,3]\) and differentiable on \((1,3)\), so MVT applies. Compute:
\[
\frac{f(3)-f(1)}{3-1}=\frac{9-1}{2}=4.
\]
Set \(f'(c)=2c=4\), get \(c=2\). Since \(2\in(1,3)\), conditions are satisfied.

entries.title: Q4. Solve \(\frac{dy}{dx}=3y\) with variable separation.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Rearrange (for \(y\neq0\), then extend to all solutions):
\[
\frac1y\,dy=3\,dx.
\]
Integrate:
\[
\int \frac1y\,dy=\int 3\,dx
\Rightarrow \ln|y|=3x+C.
\]
Exponentiate:
\[
|y|=e^{3x+C}=Ce^{3x},
\]
absorbing sign into \(C\),
\[
y=Ce^{3x}.
\]
This is the full solution family.

entries.title: Q5. Prove that if \(f'\equiv 0\) on interval \((a,b)\), then \(f\) is constant on \((a,b)\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** By Mean Value Theorem, for any \(x_1<x_2\) in \((a,b)\), there exists \(c\in(x_1,x_2)\) such that
\[
f(x_2)-f(x_1)=f'(c)(x_2-x_1).
\]
Given \(f'(c)=0\), we get \(f(x_2)-f(x_1)=0\), so \(f(x_2)=f(x_1)\). As \(x_1,x_2\) arbitrary, \(f\) is constant.

entries.title: Q6. Compute derivative of \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x}\) for \(x\neq 0\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Write \(f(x)=x^{-1}\). By power rule,
\[
f'(x)=-1\cdot x^{-2}=-\frac{1}{x^2}.
\]

entries.title: Q7. Evaluate \(\int_1^2 2x\,dx\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Antiderivative is \(x^2\), so
\[
\int_1^2 2x\,dx=[x^2]_1^2=4-1=3.
\]

entries.title: Q8. Verify FTC on \(g(x)=\int_0^x \sin t\,dt\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** By FTC, \(g'(x)=\sin x\). Compute directly from antiderivative:
\[
\int_0^x \sin t\,dt=-\cos x+\cos 0=1-\cos x,
\]
thus \(g'(x)=\sin x\). The direct derivative confirms the theorem.

entries.title: Extreme Value Theorem
entries.body: If \(f\) is continuous on a closed interval \([a,b]\), then \(f\) attains both a minimum and a maximum on \([a,b]\).

entries.title: Rolle's Theorem
entries.body: If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\), differentiable on \((a,b)\), and \(f(a)=f(b)\), then there exists \(c\in(a,b)\) such that \(f'(c)=0\).

entries.title: Lagrange Mean Value Theorem
entries.body:
If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and differentiable on \((a,b)\), then \(\exists c\in(a,b)\) with
\[
f'(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
\]

entries.title: Taylor's Theorem with Remainder, Lagrange Form
entries.body:
If \(f\) is \((n+1)\)-times differentiable on interval containing \([a,x]\), then
\[
 f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{f^{(k)}(a)}{k!}(x-a)^k + \frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi)}{(n+1)!}(x-a)^{n+1}
\]
for some \(\xi\) between \(a\) and \(x\).

entries.title: Cauchy Integral Test
entries.body: Let \((f(x))\) be positive, decreasing on \([1,\infty)\) and continuous. Then \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}f(n)\) converges iff \(\int_1^\infty f(x)\,dx\) converges.

entries.title: Q1. Extreme Value Theorem (Proof idea)
entries.body: A continuous image of a compact set is compact. \([a,b]\) is compact in \(\mathbb R\), so \(f([a,b])\) is compact, hence closed and bounded. Closed+bounded subsets of \(\mathbb R\) contain min and max values, so \(f\) attains both extrema.

entries.title: Q2. Rolle's Theorem (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Since \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\), attains max/min. If both endpoints equal, either one endpoint and nearby interior gives max/min at interior point or one endpoint dominates.
If interior extremum exists, derivative there is 0. If not, then \(f\) constant and all derivatives are 0. Therefore there exists \(c\in(a,b)\) with \(f'(c)=0\).

entries.title: Q3. Lagrange Mean Value Theorem (Proof idea)
entries.body: Define \(g(x)=f(x)-\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}(x-a)\). Then \(g(a)=g(b)\). Apply Rolle to \(g\): there exists \(c\in(a,b)\) with \(g'(c)=0\). Since \(g'(c)=f'(c)-\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}\), we get the MVT formula.

entries.title: Q4. Taylor's Theorem (Lagrange form) (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Apply the integral form recursively or apply mean-value theorem to the remainder function
\[
R_n(x)=f(x)-\sum_{k=0}^n\frac{f^{(k)}(a)}{k!}(x-a)^k.
\]
Then \(R_n^{(k)}(a)=0\) for \(k=0,\dots,n\). Repeatedly applying Rolle/MVT on suitable auxiliary functions gives
\[
R_n(x)=\frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi)}{(n+1)!}(x-a)^{n+1}
\]
for some \(\xi\in(a,x)\).

entries.title: Q5. Cauchy Integral Test (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Partition integral into unit intervals:
\[
\int_1^{\infty}f(x)dx\asymp \sum_{n\ge1}\int_n^{n+1}f(x)dx.
\]
Since \(f\) positive decreasing,
\[
\int_{n+1}^{n+2}f(x)dx\le f(n+1)\le f(x)\le f(n)\le \int_n^{n+1}f(x)dx
\]
for \(x\in[n,n+1]\). So each term compares with adjacent series terms and tail sums. Therefore convergence of one implies convergence of the other.

entries.title: Uniform Convergence
entries.body:
a sequence \\((f_n)\) of functions on \\((E\\) converges uniformly to \\(f\\) if for all \\(
\varepsilon>0\\), there exists \\N\\) such that \\(
|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\varepsilon
\) for all \\(
n\ge N\\), all \\x\in E\
\).

entries.title: Riemann Sum
entries.body:
a finite sum \\(
\sum_{i=1}^n f(c_i)\,\Delta x_i\\) approximating a definite integral.

entries.title: Arc Length
entries.body:
the length of curve \\(
\gamma:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^n\\) defined by \\(
L=\int_a^b \|\gamma'(t)\|\,dt.
\\)

entries.title: Differential Equation Initial Value
entries.body:
a differential equation together with \\(y(x_0)=y_0\
\) (and possibly higher-order initial data).

entries.title: Improper Integral at Infinity
entries.body:
a limit form \\(
\int_a^\infty f(x)\,dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\\) when the limit exists.

entries.title: Uniform Continuity
entries.body:
a function \(f\) on a set \(E\) is uniformly continuous if for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(\delta>0\) such that for all \(x,y\in E\),
\[
|x-y|<\delta \implies |f(x)-f(y)|<\varepsilon.
\]

entries.title: Improper Integral of Type II
entries.body: a limit form where the integrand is unbounded on the interval or endpoint, e.g. \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) with vertical asymptote in \((a,b)\).

entries.title: Absolute Continuity
entries.body: a stronger property than absolute continuity of measure: for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(\delta>0\) so that sums of lengths of disjoint intervals with total length <\(\delta\) force corresponding total variation of \(f\) to be <\(\varepsilon\).

entries.title: Line Integral
entries.body:
a contour sum
\[
\int_C \mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r
\]
defining work of vector field \(\mathbf F\) along curve \(C\).

entries.title: Directional Derivative
entries.body:
the derivative of \(f\) at \(x\) in unit direction \(\mathbf u\):
\[
D_{\mathbf u}f(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h\mathbf u)-f(x)}{h}.
\]

entries.title: Fourier Transform
entries.body:
For an integrable function \(f\),
\[
\mathcal F\{f\}(\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)e^{-i\omega x}\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Laplace Transform
entries.body:
For \(s\) with convergent integral,
\[
\mathcal L\{f\}(s)=\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)\,dt.
\]

entries.title: Convolution
entries.body:
The convolution of \(f,g\) is
\[
(f*g)(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)g(x-t)\,dt.
\]

entries.title: Asymptotic Order
entries.body: We write \(f(x)=O(g(x))\) as \(x\to a\) if \(|f(x)|\le C|g(x)|\) near \(a\) for some constant \(C>0\).

entries.title: Partial Differential Equation
entries.body:
An equation involving partial derivatives, such as
\[
F\!\left(x,u,\partial u,\partial^2u,\dots\right)=0,
\]
where \(\partial u\) denotes a collection of first derivatives.

entries.title: Laplace Transform
entries.body:
The **Laplace transform** of 


$f(t)$


(for 


$t\ge0$) is 


\(\mathcal L\{f\}(s)=\int_0^{\infty}e^{-st}f(t)\,dt\), where it converges.

entries.title: Inverse Laplace Transform
entries.body:
The **inverse Laplace transform** is denoted 


\(\mathcal L^{-1}\{F\}(t)\)


and satisfies 


\(\mathcal L^{-1}\{\mathcal L\{f\}\}=f\).

entries.title: Fourier Transform
entries.body:
For integrable 


$f\),


\(\widehat f(\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}f(t)e^{-i\omega t}\,dt\).

entries.title: Convolution
entries.body:
For 


$f,g\),


\((f*g)(t)=\int_0^t f(u)g(t-u)\,du\).

entries.title: Asymptotic Expansion
entries.body:
An 


**asymptotic expansion** 


\(f(x)\sim\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n\phi_n(x)\)


as 


$x\to\infty\) means 


\(f(x)-\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}a_n\phi_n(x)=o(\phi_{N}(x))\) for each fixed 


$N$.

entries.title: Complex Integral
entries.body:
For a contour 


$\gamma$


in a domain 


$\mathbb C$, the contour integral is


\[
\int_{\gamma}f(z)\,dz.

\]

entries.title: Cauchy Integral Formula
entries.body:
If 


$f\) holomorphic and 


$\gamma$


 encloses 


$a$, then


\[


f(a)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma}\frac{f(z)}{z-a}\,dz.

\]

entries.title: Residue
entries.body:
If 


$f(z)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}a_n(z-a)^n\) near isolated singularity 


$a$, then 


$\operatorname{Res}(f,a)=a_{-1}$.


The residue theorem gives


\[
\int_{\gamma}f(z)\,dz=2\pi i\sum\operatorname{Res}(f,a_k).

\]

entries.title: Contour Deformation
entries.body:
If 


$f\) is holomorphic on a homotopic region, contour integrals over homotopic paths are equal.

entries.title: Jordan's Lemma
entries.body:
For suitable decaying 


$e^{iaz}g(z)$


along semicircular arcs with 


$a>0$, the arc integral goes to zero as radius \(R\to\infty\).

entries.title: Arc Length of a Parametric Curve
entries.body:
For 


$\mathbf r(t)$


with smooth components on 


$[a,b]$, arc length is


\[
L=\int_a^b\|\mathbf r'(t)\|\,dt.

\]

entries.title: Surface of Revolution by Shells
entries.body:
The volume generated by revolving 


$y(x)$


about the y-axis is


\[V=2\pi\int_a^b x y(x)\,dx.\]

entries.title: Differentiation Under the Integral Sign
entries.body:
For smooth 


$F(x)=\int_{a(x)}^{b(x)}f(x,t)dt$,



\[
F'(x)=f(x,b(x))b'(x)-f(x,a(x))a'(x)+\int_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x,t)dt.

\]

entries.title: Asymptotic Equivalence
entries.body:
For positive functions 


$f,g$, write 


$f\sim g


\]


if 


\(\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)/g(x)=1\).

entries.title: Dominant Balance
entries.body:
For 


$\sum_i a_i(x)$,


 dominant terms are those with largest growth order as 


$x\to\infty$, giving leading asymptotic behavior.

entries.title: Laplace's Method
entries.body:
For large 


$\lambda$, integrals of the form 


\(I(\lambda)=\int_a^b e^{\lambda\phi(x)}\psi(x)\,dx\)


approximate from maxima of 


$\phi$.

entries.title: Stationary Phase Approximation
entries.body:
For oscillatory integrals


\(\int e^{i\lambda\phi(x)}a(x)\,dx\)


with large 


$\lambda$, leading behavior is driven by points where 


$\phi'(x)=0$.

entries.title: Gamma Function
entries.body:
\[
\Gamma(z)=\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}e^{-t}\,dt,\quad \Re(z)>0,
\]


generalizes factorial by 


$\Gamma(n+1)=n!$.

entries.title: Beta Function
entries.body:
\[
B(x,y)=\int_0^1 t^{x-1}(1-t)^{y-1}\,dt
\]


and


\(B(x,y)=\frac{\Gamma(x)\Gamma(y)}{\Gamma(x+y)}\).

entries.title: Saddle-Point Method
entries.body:
For contour-integral forms 


\(\int e^{\lambda f(z)}dz\),


steepest-descent paths through saddle points give asymptotic expansions.

entries.title: Riemann Sum
entries.body:
A **Riemann sum** approximates integral by
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{n} f(\xi_i)\Delta x_i.
\]

entries.title: Trapezoidal Rule
entries.body:
For partition step \(h\) on \([a,b]\),
\[
\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\approx\frac h2\big(f(x_0)+2\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}f(x_i)+f(x_n)\big).
\]

entries.title: Simpson's Rule
entries.body:
With even \(n\),
\[
\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\approx\frac h3\left[f(x_0)+4\sum_{\text{odd }i}f(x_i)+2\sum_{\text{even }i\neq0,n}f(x_i)+f(x_n)\right].
\]

entries.title: Euler-Maclaurin Formula
entries.body:
For smooth \(f\),
\[
\sum_{k=m}^n f(k)=\int_m^n f(x)\,dx+\frac{f(m)+f(n)}2+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{B_{2j}}{(2j)!}\big(f^{(2j-1)}(n)-f^{(2j-1)}(m)\big)+R_p.
\]

entries.title: Asymptotic Error Estimate
entries.body:
For method order \(p\), global error scales like \(C h^{p}\) as partition size \(h\to0\).
\[
\|E\|\le C h^{p}.
\]

entries.title: Distribution
entries.body: A **distribution** is a continuous linear functional on a space of test functions, extending classical functions.

entries.title: Dirac Delta
entries.body:
The distribution \(\delta\) satisfies
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\delta(x-a)\phi(x)\,dx=\phi(a)
\]
for any test function \(\phi\).

entries.title: Weak Derivative
entries.body:
A function \(u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) has **weak derivative** \(v\) if
\[
\int u\,\phi'=-\int v\,\phi
\]
for all smooth compactly supported test \(\phi\).

entries.title: Euler-Lagrange Equation
entries.body:
For functional
\[
J[y]=\int_a^b L(x,y,y')\,dx,
\]
critical points satisfy
\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial y}-\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial y'}\right)=0.
\]

entries.title: Functional Derivative
entries.body: For functional \(\mathcal F[f]\), a **functional derivative** \(\frac{\delta\mathcal F}{\delta f}\) gives first-order variation of \(\mathcal F\).

entries.title: Lebesgue Integral
entries.body:
For measurable \(f\), the Lebesgue integral is defined via approximation by simple functions and measure 
\(\int f\,d\mu\).

entries.title: Dominated Convergence Theorem
entries.body:
If \(f_n\to f\) pointwise and \(|f_n|\le g\) with \(\int g<\infty\), then
\(\lim_{n\to\infty}\int f_n=\int\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n.\)

entries.title: Distribution Derivative
entries.body:
The distributional derivative \(T'\) of a distribution \(T\) satisfies
\(\langle T',\varphi\rangle=-\langle T,\varphi'\rangle\) for all test functions \(\varphi\).

entries.title: Variational Derivative
entries.body:
For functional \(J[y]=\int_a^b L(x,y,y')dx\), a stationarity condition is
\(\frac{\partial L}{\partial y}-\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\partial L}{\partial y'}=0\).

entries.title: Fubini-Tonelli Theorem
entries.body:
If \(f\ge0\) or \(\int\!\int |f|<\infty\), then
\[
\int\!\left(\int f(x,y)\,dx\right)dy=\int\!\left(\int f(x,y)\,dy\right)dx.
\]

entries.title: Laplace's Method
entries.body:
For \(I(\lambda)=\int_a^b e^{\lambda\phi(x)}\psi(x)dx\) with \(\phi\) peaked at interior maximizer \(x_0\),

\[
I(\lambda)\sim e^{\lambda\phi(x_0)}\psi(x_0)\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{-\lambda\phi''(x_0)}}\quad(\lambda\to\infty).
\]

entries.title: Stationary Phase Approximation
entries.body: For oscillatory integral \(\int e^{i\lambda S(x)}a(x)dx\), main contribution comes from points where \(S'(x)=0\).

entries.title: Steepest Descent
entries.body: A contour deformation in complex plane chooses paths where\(\Im S(x)\) is constant and\(\Re S\) decreases fastest.

entries.title: Euler--Maclaurin Formula
entries.body:
For smooth \(f\),
\[
\sum_{k=a}^b f(k)=\int_a^b f(x)dx+\frac{f(a)+f(b)}2+\sum_{m=1}^{p}\frac{B_{2m}}{(2m)!}(f^{(2m-1)}(b)-f^{(2m-1)}(a))+R_p.
\]

entries.title: Mellin Transform
entries.body:
\[
\mathcal M\{f\}(s)=\int_0^{\infty}x^{s-1}f(x)\,dx,
\]
used to convert scaling into shifts in parameter \(s\).

entries.title: Euler--Lagrange Equation
entries.body:
For functional \(J[y]=\int_a^b L(x,y,y')\,dx\), stationary points satisfy
\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial y}-\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial y'}\right)=0.
\]

entries.title: First Variation
entries.body: If \(\delta J(y)[\eta]=0\) for all admissible variations \(\eta\), then \(y\) is a critical function of \(J\).

entries.title: Lagrange Multiplier (Variational Form)
entries.body:
Extrema with constraint \(\int G(x,y,y')dx=0\) satisfy augmented Euler--Lagrange equation with \(\lambda\):
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(L+\lambda G)-\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\partial}{\partial y'}(L+\lambda G)=0.
\]

entries.title: Line Integral of Vector Field
entries.body:
For path \(C\),\(
\int_C \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_a^b \mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot \mathbf r'(t)\,dt.
\)

entries.title: Green's Theorem
entries.body:
For positively oriented \(C=\partial D\),
\[
\oint_C (P\,dx+Q\,dy)=\iint_D\left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)dA.
\]

entries.title: Green's Theorem in the Plane
entries.body:
For planar region \(D\) with boundary \(\partial D\),
\[
\oint_{\partial D}(P\,dx+Q\,dy)=\iint_D\left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)dA.
\]

entries.title: Stokes' Theorem
entries.body:
For oriented surface \(S\) with boundary \(\partial S\):
\[
\oint_{\partial S}\omega=\int_S d\omega.
\]

entries.title: Divergence Theorem
entries.body:
For vector field \(\mathbf F\) on volume \(V\),
\[
\iiint_V \nabla\cdot \mathbf F\,dV=\iint_{\partial V}\mathbf F\cdot \mathbf n\,dS.
\]

entries.title: Change of Variables
entries.body:
For diffeomorphism \(\Phi\),
\[
\int_{\Phi(U)} f(y)\,dy=\int_U f(\Phi(x))\,|\det D\Phi(x)|\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Flux Through Surface
entries.body:
Flux across surface \(S\) is
\[
\iint_S \mathbf F\cdot \mathbf n\,dS,
\]
with orientation given by unit normal \(\mathbf n\).

entries.title: Laplace Transform
entries.body:
\[
\mathcal L\{f\}(s)=\int_0^\infty e^{-sx}f(x)\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Fourier Transform
entries.body:
\[
\mathcal F\{f\}(\xi)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)e^{-2\pi i\xi x}\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Convolution Theorem
entries.body:
For suitable \(f,g\),
\[
\mathcal F\{f\ast g\}=\mathcal F\{f\}\cdot \mathcal F\{g\}.
\]

entries.title: Heat Kernel
entries.body:
Solution to \(u_t=\Delta u\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) uses
\[
K_t(x)=\frac{1}{(4\pi t)^{n/2}}\exp\left(-\frac{|x|^2}{4t}\right),\quad t>0.
\]

entries.title: Green's Function
entries.body: For operator \(L\), Green's function \(G\) satisfies \(L G(x,\cdot)=\delta_x\), so \(Lu=f\) is represented via kernel integral against \(G\).

entries.title: Weak Solution
entries.body:
A function \(u\in H_0^1(\Omega)\) is a **weak solution** of
\(-\Delta u=f\) on \(\Omega\) if
\[
\int_\Omega \nabla u\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=\int_\Omega f\varphi\,dx
\]
for all test functions \(\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)\).

entries.title: Euler--Lagrange Equation (Constrained)
entries.body:
With constraint \(\int_\Omega u\,dx=c\), extremals satisfy
\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial u}-\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial u'}\right)=\lambda,
\]
with multiplier \(\lambda\).

entries.title: Lax-Milgram Theorem
entries.body:
For bounded coercive bilinear form \(a(\cdot,\cdot)\) on Hilbert space \(H\), each continuous linear functional \(f\in H'\) has unique \(u\in H\) with
\[a(u,v)=f(v)\quad\forall v\in H.\]

entries.title: Distributional Derivative Revisited
entries.body:
A locally integrable \(u\) has distributional derivative \(u'\) defined by
\(\langle u',\phi\rangle=-\langle u,\phi'\rangle\).

entries.title: Sobolev Space Norm
entries.body:
The \(H^1(\Omega)\)-norm is
\[
\|u\|_{H^1}=\left(\int_\Omega |u|^2+|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)^{1/2}.
\]

entries.title: Coarea Formula
entries.body:
For Lipschitz \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and integrable \(g\),
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n} g(x)|\nabla f(x)|dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\left(\int_{f^{-1}(t)} g\,d\sigma\right)dt.
\]

entries.title: Coarea in 2D (Polar)
entries.body:
For polar coordinates, area element
\(dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta\), yielding perimeter/area decompositions via level sets.

entries.title: BV Function
entries.body:
A function \(u\in L^1\) has bounded variation if
\(\sup\{\int u\,\mathrm{div}\,\varphi:\ \varphi\in C_c^1,\|\varphi\|_{\infty}\le1\}<\infty\).

entries.title: Hadamard Variational Formula
entries.body: For perturbed domain \(\Omega_t\), first variations of functionals are computed via boundary integrals involving normal velocity and shape derivative.

entries.title: Green’s Function (Boundary)
entries.body:
Boundary formulation writes
\(u(x)=\int_{\partial\Omega}\left(G\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}-u\frac{\partial G}{\partial n}\right)dS+\int_\Omega Gf\,dV\).

entries.title: Gâteaux Derivative
entries.body:
For \(f:V\to W\), direction \(h\) and point \(x\), the **Gâteaux derivative** is
\[
D_G f(x)(h)=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{f(x+th)-f(x)}{t},
\]
when this directional limit exists.

entries.title: Fréchet Derivative
entries.body:
The map \(f:V\to W\) is **Fréchet differentiable** at \(x\) if there is linear \(L\) with
\[
\lim_{\|h\|\to0}\frac{\|f(x+h)-f(x)-Lh\|}{\|h\|}=0.
\]

entries.title: Inverse Function Theorem
entries.body: If \(Df(x_0)\) is invertible, then \(f\) is locally a \(C^1\) bijection near \(x_0\), and \(Df^{-1}(f(x_0))=(Df(x_0))^{-1}\).

entries.title: Morse Lemma
entries.body:
If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is \(C^2\) and \(\nabla f(0)=0\), \(Hf(0)\) nonsingular, then there exists chart in which
\[
f(x)=f(0)-\sum_{i=1}^k x_i^2+\sum_{i=k+1}^{n}x_i^2.
\]

entries.title: Coarea Formula
entries.body:
For Lipschitz \(u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and integrable \(g\),
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n} g(x)\|\nabla u(x)\|\,dx=
\int_{\mathbb R}\left(\int_{u^{-1}(t)}g\,d\mathcal H^{n-1}\right)dt.
\]

entries.title: Dominated Convergence Theorem
entries.body:
If \(f_n\to f\) a.e. and \(|f_n|\le g\in L^1\), then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\int f_n=\int f.
\]

entries.title: Fubini--Tonelli Theorem
entries.body:
For nonnegative \(f\) on product spaces,
\[
\int\left(\int f(x,y)\,dy\right)\,dx
=\int\left(\int f(x,y)\,dx\right)\,dy.
\]

entries.title: Tonelli’s Theorem
entries.body: For \(\sigma\)-finite measure spaces, if \(f\ge0\), iterated integrals equal the double integral whenever one side is finite in \([0,\infty]\).

entries.title: Arzela--Ascoli Compactness
entries.body: A uniformly bounded, equicontinuous family on compact \(K\) has a uniformly convergent subsequence.

entries.title: Sobolev Space
entries.body: The Sobolev space \(W^{k,p}(\Omega)\) is the \(L^p\)-space of functions with weak derivatives up to order \(k\) in \(L^p\).

entries.title: Liouville Integrable System
entries.body: A Hamiltonian system \(\dot q=\partial H/\partial p\),\(\dot p=-\partial H/\partial q\) is Liouville integrable if it has \(n\) independent first integrals in involution.

entries.title: Poincaré--Bendixson Trichotomy
entries.body: In a planar ODE flow, every nonempty compact \(\omega\)-limit set is either fixed point, periodic orbit, or union of equilibria and orbits between them.

entries.title: Conservation Law
entries.body:
A PDE \(u_t+\nabla\cdot F(u)=0\) expresses conservation of integral quantity:
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega u\,dx= -\int_{\partial\Omega}F(u)\cdot n\,dS.
\]

entries.title: Weak-* Convergence
entries.body:
A sequence \(u_n\) converges weak-* to \(u\) in dual space if
\(\langle u_n,\varphi\rangle\to\langle u,\varphi\rangle\) for all test \(\varphi\).

entries.title: Compactness by Arzelà--Ascoli
entries.body: For equicontinuous uniformly bounded family on compact set, there exists uniformly convergent subsequence.

entries.title: Vector
entries.body: A vector in \(\mathbb R^n\) is \((v_1,\dots,v_n)\).

entries.title: Zero Vector
entries.body: The additive identity in a vector space, denoted \(\mathbf{0}\).

entries.title: Dot Product
entries.body: \(u\cdot v=\sum_{i=1}^n u_i v_i\).

entries.title: Norm
entries.body: \(\|v\|=\sqrt{v\cdot v}\).

entries.title: Vector Space
entries.body: A set with operations satisfying vector space axioms over a field.

entries.title: Subfield and Scalar
entries.body: Scalars come from a field \(\mathbb F\) in which vectors are scaled.

entries.title: Span
entries.body: \(\text{span}(S)\) is all linear combinations of vectors in \(S\).

entries.title: Linear Independence
entries.body: \(\sum c_i v_i=0\Rightarrow c_i=0\) for all \(i\).

entries.title: Basis Dimension
entries.body: Dimension is size of any basis.

entries.title: Matrix Representation
entries.body: A linear map \(T\) has matrix \([T]\) in chosen bases.

entries.title: Image
entries.body: \(\operatorname{im}(T)=\{T(v):v\in V\}\).

entries.title: Matrix Multiplication
entries.body: \((AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}\).

entries.title: Orthogonal Matrix
entries.body: \(Q^TQ=I\) implies \(Q^{-1}=Q^T\).

entries.title: Determinant
entries.body: \(\det(A)=0\) iff \(A\) is singular.

entries.title: Determinant Multiplicativity
entries.body: \(\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B)\).

entries.title: Cofactor Expansion
entries.body: \(\det(A)=\sum_j a_{ij}C_{ij}\).

entries.title: Laplace Expansion
entries.body: General recursive expansion by cofactors along a row or column.

entries.title: Gaussian Elimination
entries.body: Systematic elimination by row operations.

review.meaning: Use reversible row operations to remove coefficients and expose a linear system's solutions.
review.definition: Elimination uses row swaps, nonzero scaling and adding a multiple of a different row. Applied to whole augmented rows, these preserve the solutions. Forward elimination clears entries below successive pivots to reach echelon form. Normalizing pivots and clearing above them produces reduced row echelon form (RREF).
review.example:
[1,2|4] [3,5|11]
R2 <- R2 - 3 R1
[1,2|4] [0,-1|-1]
This is echelon form. Back-substitution gives y=1, x=2.
review.conditions: Work over a field; these examples use exact rational numbers. Never divide by zero. Update every column, including the right-hand value. A pivot is the first nonzero entry of a nonzero echelon row.
review.change: The original summary was broadly correct but omitted the allowed operations, their restrictions and the stopping forms. Some texts use Gaussian elimination for the full reduction to RREF.

sources.title: Georgia Tech: Interactive Linear Algebra, 1.2

entries.title: Reduced Row Echelon Form
entries.body: RREF gives unique canonical form by pivoting.

review.meaning: RREF is a precisely defined final matrix form. Its uniqueness does not mean that a system has exactly one solution.
review.definition: Zero rows follow all nonzero rows. Each nonzero row starts with 1; these leading 1s move strictly right as you go down. Each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column. For a fixed matrix over a field, the RREF is unique even when different legal operation sequences produce it.
review.conditions: Include the augmented column when checking the form. A row [0,0|1] means no solution. A consistent system with a free variable has multiple solutions over the rationals. A consistent system with a pivot for every variable has one solution.
review.change: The original uniqueness statement needed the defining conditions and the distinction between a unique matrix form and a unique solution. RREF does not require a square or invertible matrix.
review.source_body: RREF gives unique canonical form by pivoting.

entries.title: Rank
entries.body: Dimension of column space.

review.meaning: Rank counts independent columns. Comparing the ranks of A and [A|b] tells whether Ax=b has a solution.
review.definition: For a matrix A over a field, rank(A) is the dimension of its column space. It also equals the dimension of its row space and the number of pivots after row reduction. In Ax=b, A contains only the variable coefficients; [A|b] includes the right-hand column. The system is consistent (has at least one solution) exactly when rank(A)=rank([A|b]).
review.example:
[1,2|3] [2,4|7]
R2 <- R2 - 2 R1 gives [1,2|3] [0,0|1].
rank(A)=1; rank([A|b])=2: no solution.
Change 7 to 6: both ranks are 1, with infinitely many rational solutions.
review.conditions: For m equations in n unknowns, A has m rows and n columns; b is not an unknown. Appending b leaves the rank unchanged exactly when b lies in the column space of A. If consistent, rank(A)=n gives one solution; rank(A)<n gives n-rank(A) free variables and infinitely many solutions over the rationals or reals. A reduced augmented row [0,...,0|c] with c nonzero means no solution, even if A has a pivot in every variable column.
review.change: The original column-space definition is correct but too brief to connect rank to solving. This adaptation adds the row/pivot interpretations and distinguishes coefficient rank from augmented rank. The equality-of-ranks criterion follows from the cited column-span consistency criterion: adding b changes the span dimension precisely when b is outside it.

entries.title: Nullity
entries.body: Dimension of kernel; \(\text{rank} + \text{nullity}=\dim V\).

review.meaning: Nullity counts independent directions that A sends to zero, and the free parameters available when Ax=b is consistent.
review.definition: For an m by n matrix A over a field, its kernel (null space) is the set of vectors x with Ax=0. Nullity is the dimension of that space. Rank-nullity says rank(A)+nullity(A)=n, the number of coefficient columns. In a consistent system, variables whose columns have no pivot in echelon form are free: they may be chosen independently, and the pivot variables follow from the equations.
review.example:
[1,0,2|5] [0,1,-1|1]
rank(A)=2; nullity(A)=3-2=1.
z=t; x=5-2t; y=1+t.
All rational solutions: (5,1,0)+t(-2,1,1).
The kernel is spanned by (-2,1,1).
review.conditions: The formula uses the finite dimension of the domain: n unknowns, excluding the augmented column. For consistent Ax=b, every solution is a particular solution plus a vector in the kernel; n-rank(A) counts its free parameters. Nullity(A) remains defined if Ax=b is inconsistent, but then there is no solution family to parameterize. A positive nullity gives infinitely many solutions only over an infinite field such as the rationals or reals, and only when consistent.
review.change: The original kernel definition and rank-nullity identity are correct for a finite-dimensional linear map, but omit that assumption and what dim V counts. This adaptation makes the matrix domain explicit and connects nonpivot variable columns to free parameters, without treating the right-hand column as a variable or promising solutions for an inconsistent system.

entries.body: Pairwise orthogonal with unit norm vectors.

entries.title: Orthogonal Projection
entries.body: \(\text{proj}_v(u)=\frac{u\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v\).

entries.title: Gram-Schmidt

entries.title: Eigenpair

entries.title: Characteristic Polynomial
