entries.title: Algebraic Multiplicity
entries.body: Multiplicity of eigenvalue as root multiplicity of characteristic polynomial.

entries.title: Diagonalizable
entries.body: \(A=PDP^{-1}\) with diagonal \(D\).

entries.title: Singular Value Decomposition
entries.body: \(A=U\Sigma V^\top\) with orthogonal/unitary factors.

entries.title: Rank-Nullity Theorem
entries.body: \(\dim V = \dim\ker T + \dim\operatorname{im}T\).

entries.title: Rank-Nullity
entries.body:
For linear map \(T:V\to W\) with \(\dim V=n\):
\[
\operatorname{rank}(T)+\operatorname{nullity}(T)=n.
\]

entries.title: Determinant and Invertibility
entries.body: A square matrix \(A\) is invertible iff \(\det(A)\neq 0\).

entries.title: Spectral Decomposition Criterion
entries.body: If matrix \(A\) has \(n\) linearly independent eigenvectors, then \(A\) is diagonalizable.

entries.title: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
entries.body:
For \(u,v\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
|u\cdot v|\le \|u\|\,\|v\|,
\]
and equality holds iff \(u\) and \(v\) are linearly dependent.

entries.title: Find Inverse of a Matrix
entries.body:
For
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad \det(A)=1\neq 0,
\]
so
\[
A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

entries.title: Rank-Nullity
entries.body:
For \(T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2\) with matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
rank is 2, so nullity is \(3-2=1\).
Kernel is spanned by \((0,0,1)\).

entries.title: Dot Product Orthogonality
entries.body:
For \(u=(1,2,2)\), \(v=(2,-1,1)\):
\[
u\cdot v=1\cdot2+2\cdot(-1)+2\cdot1=2-2+2=2.\]
Hence not orthogonal.

entries.title: Eigenpair
entries.body:
For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}\),
\(\lambda_1=2\), \(\lambda_2=3\) with eigenvectors \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\).
\(A\) is already diagonal.

entries.title: Q1. Prove that \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\) is invertible and find \(A^{-1}\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Compute determinant:
\[
\det A=1\cdot1-0\cdot2=1\neq0.
\]
Nonzero determinant is equivalent to invertibility for square matrices. So \(A^{-1}\) exists and is
\[
\frac{1}{\det A}\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Check:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=I.
\]

entries.title: Q2. Compute rank and nullity of
entries.body:
\(T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2\) with matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}\).

**Answer.** The two pivot columns are the first two, so rank is 2. By rank-nullity with domain dimension 3,
\[
\text{nullity}=3-\text{rank}=1.
\]
Indeed kernel equations are \(x_1=0, x_2=0\); free variable \(x_3\) gives vectors \((0,0,t)\), a one-dimensional kernel.

entries.title: Q3. Show \(u=(1,2,2)\) and \(v=(2,-1,1)\) are not orthogonal.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Compute dot product:
\[
u\cdot v=1\cdot2+2\cdot(-1)+2\cdot1=2-2+2=2\neq0.
\]
Since orthogonality requires dot product zero, \(u\) and \(v\) are not orthogonal.

entries.title: Q4. Find eigenpairs of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** For diagonal matrix, action is coordinate-wise scaling:
\[
A(1,0)^T=(2,0)^T=2(1,0)^T,
\qquad
A(0,1)^T=(0,3)^T=3(0,1)^T.
\]
So eigenpairs are \((\lambda,v)=(2,(1,0)^T)\) and \((3,(0,1)^T)\). Matrix is already diagonal, so diagonalization is trivial with \(P=I\), \(D=A\).

entries.title: Q5. Show the vectors \((1,0,0)\), \((0,1,0)\), \((0,0,1)\) form a basis for \(\mathbb R^3\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Let \((a,b,c)\in\mathbb R^3\) and consider
\[
a(1,0,0)+b(0,1,0)+c(0,0,1)=(a,b,c).
\]
Every vector in \(\mathbb R^3\) is represented with unique coefficients \((a,b,c)\), so the set spans and is independent; hence it is a basis.

entries.title: Q6. Prove vectors are orthogonal implies dot product is zero.
entries.body: **Answer.** By definition of orthogonality in Euclidean inner-product spaces, \(u\perp v\) means angle is \(90^\circ\). For angle \(\theta\),\(u\cdot v=\|u\|\|v\|\cos\theta\). With \(\theta=\pi/2\), \(\cos\theta=0\), so \(u\cdot v=0\).

entries.title: Q7. Compute \(\det\) of upper triangular matrix.
entries.body:
**Answer.** For 
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}3&4&1\\0&2&-1\\0&0&5\end{pmatrix},
\]
determinant is product of diagonal entries:
\[
\det(A)=3\cdot2\cdot5=30.
\]
Hence \(A\) is invertible.

entries.title: Q8. Verify \(\operatorname{rank} A + \operatorname{nullity} A = \dim(\mathbb R^3)\) for a simple map.
entries.body:
**Answer.** Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad T(x)=Ax.
\]
Two pivot columns imply rank 2. Since domain is \(\mathbb R^3\), nullity is \(3-2=1\).
Then
\[
\operatorname{rank}(T)+\operatorname{nullity}(T)=2+1=3=\dim\mathbb R^3.
\]
This matches rank-nullity.

entries.title: Existence of Basis
entries.body: Every vector space \(V\) over a field \(F\) has a basis.

entries.title: Dimension Formula for Direct Sum
entries.body:
If \(U,W\subseteq V\) are subspaces with \(U\cap W=\{0\}\), then
\[
\dim(U\oplus W)=\dim U+\dim W.
\]

entries.title: Cayley-Hamilton Theorem
entries.body:
For \(A\in M_n(F)\), if \(p_A(t)=\det(tI-A)\) is the characteristic polynomial, then
\[
p_A(A)=0
\]
(the zero matrix).

entries.title: Spectral Theorem for Real Symmetric Matrices
entries.body: If \(A\) is a real symmetric matrix, then \(A\) is diagonalizable by an orthogonal matrix: there exists orthogonal \(Q\) such that \(Q^TAQ=\Lambda\) is diagonal with real entries.

entries.title: Cauchy-Binet Formula
entries.body:
For \(A\in M_{m\times n}\), \(B\in M_{n\times m}\),
\[
\det(AB)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\},\,|S|=m}\det(A_{[:,S]})\det(B_{[S,:]}).
\]
\(A_{[:,S]}\) and \(B_{[S,:]}\) denote selected-column/row submatrices.

entries.title: Q1. Existence of a Basis (Proof idea)
entries.body:
For vector space \(V\), consider set of linearly independent subsets ordered by inclusion. Chains have upper bounds via unions. By Zorn's Lemma, there exists a maximal linearly independent set \(B\). Maximality implies it spans \(V\), otherwise one could adjoin a nonspanned vector and remain independent.
Hence \(B\) is a basis.

entries.title: Q2. Dimension formula for direct sum (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Assume \(U\cap W=\{0\}\). Let \(\{u_1,\dots,u_m\}\) be a basis of \(U\) and \(\{w_1,\dots,w_n\}\) be a basis of \(W\).
Any vector in \(U\oplus W\) is written uniquely as \(u+w\), and can be written
\[
\sum_i \alpha_i u_i + \sum_j \beta_j w_j.
\]
Independence: if this sum is 0 then \(\sum_i \alpha_i u_i = -\sum_j \beta_j w_j\in U\cap W=\{0\}\), so both sides zero and coefficients vanish. So concatenation is a basis. Size is \(m+n\).

entries.title: Q3. Cayley-Hamilton (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Let \(A\in M_n(F)\), \(p_A(t)=\det(tI-A)=t^n+c_1t^{n-1}+\cdots+c_n\). Define adjugate matrix \(\operatorname{adj}(tI-A)\). Identity:
\[
\operatorname{adj}(tI-A)(tI-A)=p_A(t)I.
\]
Substitute matrix argument \(t=A\):
\[
\operatorname{adj}(AI-A)(AI-A)=\operatorname{adj}(0)(0)=p_A(A)I.
\]
Since \(AI-A=0\), left side is zero, hence \(p_A(A)=0\).

entries.title: Q4. Spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices (Proof idea)
entries.body:
For real symmetric \(A\), characteristic polynomial has at least one real eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and unit eigenvector \(v\). Decompose
\[
\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{span}\{v\}\oplus v^\perp.
\]
Space \(v^\perp\) is \(A\)-invariant. Apply induction on dimension to get orthonormal eigenbasis of \(v^\perp\), then add \(v\). Construct orthogonal \(Q\) with these basis vectors as columns so \(Q^TAQ\) is diagonal.

entries.title: Q5. Cauchy-Binet (Proof idea)
entries.body:
\(\det(AB)\) for \(m\times m\) product expanded as multilinear alternating form in columns of \(AB\). Replacing each column by linear combinations of columns of \(A\) with coefficients from \(B\) yields sum over all \(m\)-index subsets \(S\) of columns:
\[
\det(AB)=\sum_{|S|=m}\det(A_{[:,S]})\det(B_{[S,:]}).
\]
All other repeated-column terms vanish by alternation, leaving exactly these minors.

entries.title: Affine Subspace
entries.body: a set \\(v+W=\{v+w\mid w\in W\}\) where \\(W\subseteq V\) is a subspace and \\(v\in V\).

entries.title: Column Space
entries.body: the subspace \\(\mathcal{C}(A)=\{Ax\mid x\in\mathbb F^n\}\subseteq\mathbb F^m\\) for an \\m\times n\\) matrix \\A.

entries.title: Left Null Space
entries.body:
the null space of \\(^T\!
A\): \\(
\{y\in\mathbb F^m\mid y^TA=0\}.
\\)

entries.title: Orthogonal Complement
entries.body: the set \\(W^\perp=\{v\mid v\cdot w=0\ \forall w\in W\}\).

entries.title: Symmetric Matrix
entries.body: a matrix \\(A\\) with \\(A^T=A\).

entries.title: Adjugate Matrix
entries.body:
the matrix of cofactors transposed, satisfying
\[
A\,\operatorname{adj}(A)=\det(A)I.
\]

entries.title: Trace
entries.body:
the sum of diagonal entries of a square matrix:
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A)=\sum_i a_{ii}.
\]

entries.title: Jordan Normal Form
entries.body: a block-diagonal canonical form composed of Jordan blocks, similar to a matrix over algebraically closed fields.

entries.title: Bilinear Form
entries.body: a map \(B:V\times V\to\mathbb F\) linear in each argument separately.

entries.title: Gram Matrix
entries.body: the matrix \(G=(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)_{ij}\) associated with vectors \(v_1,\dots,v_n\).

entries.title: Singular Value Decomposition
entries.body:
Every real matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has factorization
\[
A=U\Sigma V^\top
\]
with \(U,V\) orthogonal and \(\Sigma\) diagonal nonnegative.

entries.title: Orthogonal Projection
entries.body: Projection onto a subspace \(W\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the linear map \(P_W\) with \(P_W^2=P_W\), \(P_W^T=P_W\), and \(P_W v=v\) for \(v\in W\).

entries.title: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse
entries.body: For a matrix \(A\), the pseudoinverse \(A^\dagger\) is the unique matrix satisfying \(AA^\dagger A=A\), \(A^\dagger A A^\dagger=A^\dagger\), and symmetry conditions on \(AA^\dagger\) and \(A^\dagger A\).

entries.title: QR Decomposition
entries.body: Any full matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) can be written as \(A=QR\), with orthogonal \(Q\) and upper-triangular \(R\).

entries.title: Spectral Radius
entries.body:
The spectral radius of \(A\) is
\[
\rho(A)=\max\{|\lambda|\mid \lambda\in\sigma(A)\},
\]
the maximum absolute eigenvalue.

entries.title: Bilinear Form
entries.body:
A **bilinear form** on a vector space 


$V$


over 


$\mathbb F\) is a map 


$B:V\times V\to\mathbb F$


linear in each argument.

entries.title: Quadratic Form
entries.body:
A **quadratic form** is a map 


$q:V\to\mathbb F\) of the form 


$q(v)=B(v,v)\) for some bilinear form 


$B$.

entries.title: Linear Functional
entries.body:
A **linear functional** is a linear map 


$f:V\to\mathbb F\).


A linear functional belongs to the dual space 


$V^*=\mathrm{Hom}(V,\mathbb F)$.

entries.title: Tensor Product of Vector Spaces
entries.body:
For spaces 


$V,W$, the **tensor product** 


$V\otimes W$


is the universal bilinear target supporting 


$V\times W\to V\otimes W$.

entries.title: Adjoint Operator
entries.body:
For inner-product spaces and 


$T:V\to V$,


its **adjoint** 


$T^*\) satisfies 


$\langle Tv,w\rangle=\langle v,T^*w\rangle$.

entries.title: Normed Vector Space
entries.body:
A vector space 


$V$


with norm 


$\|\cdot\|:V\to[0,\infty)$


satisfying positivity, homogeneity, and triangle inequality is a **normed vector space**.

entries.title: Inner Product Space
entries.body:
A **inner product space** has map 


$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:V\times V\to\mathbb F$


that is conjugate-symmetric, linear in first slot, and positive-definite.

entries.title: Banach Space
entries.body:
A normed vector space is a 


**Banach space** if it is complete in the norm metric 


$d(u,v)=\|u-v\|$.

entries.title: Hilbert Space
entries.body:
A Banach space whose norm comes from an inner product is a 


**Hilbert space**.

entries.title: Compact Operator
entries.body:
A bounded linear operator 


$T:X\to Y$


is **compact** when it sends bounded sets to relatively compact sets.

entries.title: Singular Value Decomposition
entries.body:
Any matrix 


$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$


factors as


\[A=U\Sigma V^T\]


with orthogonal 


$U,V$ and diagonal singular values in 


$\Sigma$.

entries.title: QR Decomposition
entries.body:
For 


$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, 


**QR decomposition** writes 


$A=QR$ with orthonormal 


$Q$ and upper-triangular 


$R$.

entries.title: LU Decomposition
entries.body:
**LU decomposition** expresses a matrix as


\(A=LU\)


with 


$L$ lower triangular, 


$U$ upper triangular (under pivot conditions).

entries.title: Cholesky Decomposition
entries.body:
For positive definite 


$A$, 


\(A=LL^T\)


with lower triangular 


$L$ and positive diagonal entries.

entries.title: Polar Decomposition
entries.body:
Every square 


$A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$


can be written as 


\(A=UP\)


with orthogonal 


$U$ and symmetric positive semidefinite 


$P$.

entries.title: Normal Operator
entries.body:
An operator 


$T\) on inner product space is **normal** if 


$TT^*=T^*T$.

entries.title: Self-Adjoint Operator
entries.body:
a linear operator 


$T$ is **self-adjoint** if 


$T=T^*$.

entries.title: Unitary Operator
entries.body:
$U$ is **unitary** if 


$U^*U=UU^*=I$.

entries.title: Orthogonal Projection Operator
entries.body:
For closed subspace 


$W\subset V$, 


$P_W^2=P_W$, 


$P_W^*=P_W$, and 


$\operatorname{im}P_W=W$.

entries.title: Functional Calculus for Normal Operators
entries.body:
If 


$T$ is normal and diagonalizable via spectral theorem, one may define 


$f(T)$


for suitable Borel/continuous functions 


$f$ on its spectrum.

entries.title: Bounded Operator
entries.body:
A linear operator \(T:X\to Y\) is **bounded** if there exists \(C\ge0\) such that
\[
\|Tx\|\le C\|x\|\quad\forall x\in X.
\]

entries.title: Operator Norm
entries.body:
The **operator norm** of bounded \(T\) is
\[
\|T\|=\sup_{\|x\|=1}\|Tx\|.
\]

entries.title: Spectrum
entries.body:
For operator \(T\), its **spectrum** is
\[
\sigma(T)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb C: T-\lambda I\text{ not invertible}\}.
\]

entries.title: Resolvent
entries.body:
The **resolvent set** is
\[
\rho(T)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb C: (T-\lambda I)^{-1}\text{ exists and is bounded}\},
\]
and resolvent is \(R(\lambda,T)=(T-\lambda I)^{-1}\).

entries.title: Fredholm Operator
entries.body: A bounded operator \(T\) is **Fredholm** if both kernel and cokernel are finite-dimensional and \(\operatorname{im}T\) is closed.

entries.title: Index of Fredholm Operator
entries.body:
For Fredholm \(T\), 
\(
\mathrm{ind}(T)=\dim\ker T-\dim\ker T^*.
\)

entries.title: Tensor Product
entries.body: For vector spaces \(V,W\), the **tensor product** \(V\otimes W\) is universal for bilinear maps from \(V\times W\).

entries.title: Exterior Product
entries.body: The **exterior product** \(v\wedge w\) is alternating, with \(v\wedge v=0\), and extends to exterior powers \(\Lambda^k V\).

entries.title: Symmetric Power
entries.body: The **symmetric power** \(\mathrm{Sym}^k(V)\) is the quotient of \(V^{\otimes k}\) by swapping factor permutations.

entries.title: Multilinear Map
entries.body: A map \(T:V_1\times\cdots\times V_k\to W\) is **multilinear** when linear in each argument separately.

entries.title: Tensor Contraction
entries.body: **Tensor contraction** pairs one covariant and one contravariant index, reducing tensor order by 2.

entries.title: Kronecker Product
entries.body:
For matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\),
\(A\otimes B\in\mathbb R^{mp\times nq}\) stacks scaled blocks \(a_{ij}B\).

entries.title: Tensor Rank
entries.body:
The tensor rank of \(\mathcal T\) is the minimum \(r\) such that
\(\mathcal T=\sum_{i=1}^r u_i\otimes v_i\otimes w_i\).

entries.title: Tensor Contraction
entries.body: Contraction is an index summation reducing order, e.g. from \(T_{ijk}\) to \(A_{jk}=\sum_i T_{ijk}u_i\).

entries.title: Schur Complement
entries.body:
For block matrix
\(\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}\), if \(A\) invertible, then
\(S=D-CA^{-1}B\) is its Schur complement.

entries.title: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse
entries.body: \(A^+\) satisfies \(AA^+A=A\), \(A^+AA^+=A^+\), and minimal-norm least squares properties.

entries.title: Polar Decomposition
entries.body: For bounded operator \(T\),\(T=U|T|\) with partial isometry \(U\) and \(|T|=(T^*T)^{1/2}\).

entries.title: Functional Calculus
entries.body: For normal operator \(A\), continuous \(f\) defines \(f(A)\) by spectral theorem.

entries.title: C*-Algebra
entries.body: A Banach *-algebra \(A\) with \(\|a^*a\|=\|a\|^2\) for all \(a\).

entries.title: Polar Decomposition of Matrices
entries.body: Any matrix \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}\) has \(A=U\Sigma V^*\) (SVD), separating unitary and positive-semidefinite parts.

entries.title: Canonical Polyadic Decomposition
entries.body:
A tensor \(\mathcal T\) is written as a sum of rank-one terms
\(\mathcal T=\sum_{r=1}^R a_r\circ b_r\circ c_r\).

entries.title: Polar Decomposition
entries.body: For any complex matrix \(A\), there exists \(A=UP\) with unitary \(U\) and positive semidefinite \(P=\sqrt{A^*A}\).

entries.title: Functional Calculus (Self-Adjoint)
entries.body:
If \(A\) is symmetric and diagonalizable \(A=Q\Lambda Q^T\), then for polynomial/continuous \(f\),
\(f(A)=Qf(\Lambda)Q^T\).

entries.title: Spectral Radius
entries.body:
\(
\rho(A)=\max\{||:\lambda\in\sigma(A)\}
\)
is the radius of smallest disk centered at origin containing spectrum.

entries.title: Numerical Range
entries.body: The numerical range of \(A\) is \(W(A)=\{x^*Ax:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(\sigma(A)\subseteq \overline{W(A)}\).

entries.title: Schur Decomposition
entries.body: Every square \(A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\) factors as \(A=UTU^*\) with \(U\) unitary and \(T\) upper triangular.

entries.title: QR Decomposition
entries.body: Any full-rank matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) can be written as \(A=QR\) where \(Q\) has orthonormal columns and \(R\) is upper triangular.

entries.title: Cholesky Decomposition
entries.body:
For symmetric positive-definite \(A\), there exists unique lower triangular \(L\) with
\(A=LL^T\).

entries.title: Jordan Canonical Form
entries.body:
For linear map \(T\), there is basis with block-diagonal
\(J\) (Jordan form) such that \(A=PJP^{-1}\).

entries.title: Singular Values
entries.body: Singular values \(\sigma_i\) are square roots of eigenvalues of \(A^TA\), sorted \(\sigma_1\ge\dots\ge\sigma_r\ge0\).

entries.title: Numerical Condition Number
entries.body: For invertible \(A\),\(\kappa(A)=\|A\|\,\|A^{-1}\|\), measuring sensitivity of linear solves.

entries.title: Hessenberg Reduction
entries.body: Any matrix can be orthogonally transformed to Hessenberg form for efficient eigenvalue computation.

entries.title: Bidiagonal Decomposition
entries.body: Any matrix \(A\) admits \(A=U B V^*\) with orthogonal/unitary \(U,V\) and bidiagonal \(B\) (via Golub-Kahan).

entries.title: Householder Reflection
entries.body:
A Householder matrix has form
\(H=I-2\frac{uu^*}{u^*u}\) and reflects vectors across a hyperplane.

entries.title: Givens Rotation
entries.body:
A Givens rotation
\(
G(i,j,\theta)
\)
annihilates a chosen coordinate while preserving orthogonality via local \(2\times2\) plane rotation.

entries.title: Cosine-Sine Decomposition
entries.body: For unitary \(U\), CSD writes \(U\) via cosine-sine blocks and principal angles between subspaces.

entries.title: Operator Norm
entries.body:
For linear \(T\) on a normed space,
\[
\|T\|=\sup_{\|x\|\le1}\|Tx\|.
\]

entries.title: Resolvent Set
entries.body:
For operator \(A\), resolvent set
\(\rho(A)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb C:(\lambda I-A)^{-1}\text{ exists and bounded}\}\).

entries.title: Spectral Radius Formula
entries.body:
For bounded operator \(A\),
\[
\rho(A)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\|A^n\|^{1/n}.
\]

entries.title: Compact Operator
entries.body: A bounded linear operator \(K\) is **compact** if it maps unit balls to relatively compact sets.

entries.title: Fredholm Alternative
entries.body: For compact \(K\), either \((I-K)u=f\) is uniquely solvable for all \(f\), or homogeneous equation has nonzero solutions and compatibility conditions are required.

entries.title: Perturbation Theory
entries.body: For matrix \(A+\epsilon B\), eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and conditionally spectral data vary with \(\epsilon\), with first-order perturbation formulas.

entries.title: Bauer-Fike Bound
entries.body:
If \(A=V\Lambda V^{-1}\), then every eigenvalue \(\mu\) of \(A+E\) satisfies
\(
\min_j|\mu-\lambda_j|\le \kappa(V)\|E\|.
\)

entries.title: Pseudospectrum
entries.body:
The \(\epsilon\)-pseudospectrum is
\(\Lambda_\epsilon(A)=\{z:\|(zI-A)^{-1}\|>\epsilon^{-1}\}\cup\sigma(A)\).

entries.title: Structured Backward Error
entries.body: Given \(\widetilde\lambda\), backward error is smallest \(\delta A\) with \(\widetilde\lambda\in\sigma(A+\delta A)\), measuring robustness of computed eigenpairs.

entries.title: Wedin's \(\sin\theta\) Theorem
entries.body: For perturbed matrix \(A+E\), canonical angles \(\theta_i\) between singular subspaces satisfy bounds by \(\|E\|ig/\delta\), where \(\delta\) is spectral gap.

entries.title: Davis--Kahan Theorem
entries.body:
If \(A\) is symmetric and \(\lambda\) isolated, perturbation of eigenvectors is bounded by
\[
\sin\theta\le \frac{\|E\|_2}{\mathrm{gap}}.
\]

entries.title: Principal Angles
entries.body:
For subspaces \(\mathcal U,\mathcal V\), principal angles \(\theta_i\) are defined recursively via 
\(\cos\theta_i=\max_{u\in\mathcal U,v\in\mathcal V}\langle u,v\rangle\), orthogonalizing each step.

entries.title: Subspace Distance
entries.body:
The distance between subspaces can be measured by
\(
\|P_{\mathcal U}-P_{\mathcal V}\|_2=\sin\theta_{\max}.
\)

entries.title: Procrustes Problem
entries.body: Given \(A,B\), minimize \(\|A-RB\|_F\) over orthogonal \(R\); solution uses SVD of \(AB^T\).

entries.title: Polar Decomposition
entries.body: Every matrix \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}\) has \(A=UP\), where \(U\) is partial unitary and \(P\) is positive semidefinite.

entries.title: QR Decomposition
entries.body: A full-rank matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has \(A=QR\), with \(Q^TQ=I\) and \(R\) upper triangular.

entries.title: Schur Decomposition
entries.body: Over \(\mathbb C\), \(A=QTQ^*\) where \(Q\) is unitary and \(T\) is upper triangular.

entries.title: Jordan Canonical Form
entries.body: If \(A\) is similar to \(PJP^{-1}\), then \(J\) is block diagonal with Jordan blocks \(J_k(\lambda)\) and \(A\) and \(J\) share characteristic polynomial.

entries.title: Smith Normal Form
entries.body: For integer matrix \(A\), unimodular \(U,V\) give \(UAV=\mathrm{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_r,0,\dots,0)\) with \(d_i|d_{i+1}\).

entries.title: Unitary Matrix
entries.body: A matrix \(U\) is unitary if \(U^*U=I\), equivalently \(\|Ux\|_2=\|x\|_2\) for all vectors \(x\).

entries.title: Unitary Congruence
entries.body: Matrices \(A,B\) are **unitarily congruent** if \(B=U^T A U\) for some unitary \(U\).

entries.title: Unitary Equivalence
entries.body: Matrices \(A,B\) are unitarily equivalent if \(B=UAU^*\) for some unitary \(U\).

entries.title: Numerical Range
entries.body: The **numerical range** is \(\{x^*Ax:\|x\|_2=1\}\), a convex subset of \(\mathbb C\).

entries.title: Rayleigh Quotient
entries.body: For Hermitian \(A\), \(R_A(x)=\frac{x^*Ax}{x^*x}\); its extrema over nonzero \(x\) are min/max eigenvalues.

entries.title: Proposition
entries.body: A truth-valued statement.

entries.title: Negation
entries.body: \(\neg p\) reverses the truth of \(p\).

entries.title: Conjunction
entries.body: \(p\wedge q\) is true iff both \(p\) and \(q\) are true.

entries.title: Logical Equivalence
entries.body: \(P\iff Q\).

entries.title: Proof by Contradiction
entries.body: Assume negation, derive contradiction, conclude statement.

entries.title: Union
entries.body: \(A\cup B=\{x\mid x\in A\lor x\in B\}\).

entries.title: Intersection
entries.body: \(A\cap B=\{x\mid x\in A\land x\in B\}\).

entries.title: Cartesian Product
entries.body: \(A\times B=\{(a,b):a\in A,b\in B\}\).

entries.title: Equivalence Relation
entries.body: Reflexive, symmetric, transitive.

entries.title: Function
entries.body: A special relation assigning one codomain element to each domain element.

entries.title: Bijection
entries.body: Injective and surjective function.

entries.title: Binomial Coefficient
entries.body: \({n\choose k}=\frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}\).

entries.title: Combination with Repetition
entries.body: \({n+k-1\choose k}\) gives multisets.

entries.title: Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
entries.body: \(|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|\).

entries.title: Catalan Count (Contextual)
entries.body: \(C_n=\frac1{n+1}{2n\choose n}\) counts balanced parenthesis strings.

entries.title: Graph
entries.body: \((V,E)\) with vertices and edges.

entries.title: Subgraph
entries.body: A graph formed by subsets of vertices and edges.

entries.title: Eulerian Path
entries.body: Path using each edge exactly once.

entries.title: Hamiltonian Cycle
entries.body: Cycle visiting every vertex exactly once.

entries.title: Divisibility
entries.body: \(a\mid b\iff \exists k\in\mathbb Z: b=ka\).

entries.title: Prime Factorization
entries.body: Every \(n>1\) factors uniquely into primes up to order.

entries.title: Congruence
entries.body: \(a\equiv b\pmod n\iff n\mid(a-b)\).

entries.title: Euler's Totient
entries.body: \(\varphi(n)\) counts \(1\le k\le n\) coprime to \(n\).

entries.title: Recurrence Relation
entries.body: \(a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}\) is a sample second-order recurrence.

entries.title: Linear Homogeneous Recurrence
entries.body: Form \(a_n=c_1a_{n-1}+\cdots+c_k a_{n-k}\).

entries.title: Strong Induction
entries.body: Assume statement true for all \(k\le n\) to prove for \(n+1\).

entries.title: Induction on Two Parameters
entries.body: Nested base and step proving on pairs \((m,n)\).

entries.title: Theta and Omega
entries.body: \(f=\Theta(g)\) and \(f=\Omega(g)\) denote tight/lower bounds.

entries.title: Polynomial Time
entries.body: \(T(n)=O(n^k)\) for some \(k\).

entries.title: Exponential Time
entries.body: \(T(n)=O(a^n)\), typically much slower than polynomial.

entries.title: Disjunction
entries.body: \(p\vee q\).

entries.title: Exclusive Or
entries.body: \(p\oplus q\) true exactly when exactly one is true.

entries.title: Implication
entries.body: \(p\to q\) is false only when \(p\) true and \(q\) false.

entries.title: Biconditional
entries.body: \(p\iff q\).

entries.title: Pigeonhole Principle
entries.body: If \(n\) objects are placed into \(m\) boxes and \(n>m\), then at least one box contains at least two objects.

entries.title: Inclusion–Exclusion for Two Sets
entries.body:
For finite sets \(A,B\):
\[
|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|.
\]

entries.title: Euler's Theorem in Number Theory
entries.body:
If \(\gcd(a,n)=1\), then
\[
a^{\varphi(n)}\equiv 1\pmod n,
\]
where \(\varphi\) is Euler's totient.

entries.title: Handshake Lemma
entries.body:
In any finite graph, sum of degrees equals twice number of edges:
\[
\sum_{v\in V}\deg(v)=2|E|.
\]

entries.title: Pigeonhole Application
entries.body: Among 13 integers, at least two have the same remainder when divided by 12.

entries.title: Handshaking Count
entries.body:
For triangle graph with \(3\) edges,
\[\deg(v_1)=\deg(v_2)=\deg(v_3)=2\]
so \(\sum\deg=6=2|E|\) consistent with theorem.

entries.title: Q1. Apply the Pigeonhole Principle to 13 numbers into 12 remainder classes mod 12.
entries.body: **Answer.** The remainders mod 12 are \(0,1,\dots,11\): 12 boxes. Placing 13 integers into 12 boxes, by pigeonhole at least one box has at least two integers. Hence two integers have the same remainder mod 12.

entries.title: Q2. Compute \(|A\cup B|\) from \(|A|=10\), \(|B|=8\), \(|A\cap B|=3\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** Use inclusion-exclusion:
\[
|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|=10+8-3=15.
\]
So the union has 15 distinct elements.

entries.title: Q3. Verify Euler theorem for \(a=3, n=10\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** First \(\gcd(3,10)=1\), so theorem applies. Compute \(\varphi(10)=4\). Then
\[
3^4=81\equiv1\pmod{10},
\]
since \(81-1=80\) is divisible by 10.

entries.title: Q4. Check handshake lemma on triangle graph.
entries.body:
**Answer.** A triangle has \(3\) edges. Each edge contributes degree \(+2\) total across endpoints, so total degree should be \(2\cdot3=6\).
Directly, each of 3 vertices has degree 2:
\[
\sum_{v\in V}\deg(v)=2+2+2=6.
\]
Both sides match, so lemma holds.

entries.title: Q5. Prove inclusion-exclusion for finite sets with \(A\cap B=\varnothing\).
entries.body:
**Answer.** If \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), then \(|A\cap B|=0\). Substituting into inclusion-exclusion:
\[
|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|=|A|+|B|-0=|A|+|B|,
\]
which is exactly disjoint union cardinality.

entries.title: Q6. Show there is no graph on 3 vertices with 4 edges.
entries.body:
**Answer.** A simple graph with 3 vertices has at most \(\binom{3}{2}=3\) edges (all pairs).
So 4 edges is impossible because that would require multiple edges between some vertex pair, i.e., not simple. Hence no such simple graph.

entries.title: Q7. Compute \(5\)th Fibonacci number by recurrence.
Q8. Prove \(\sum_{v\in V}\deg(v)=2|E|\) for square graph.
entries.body:
**Answer.** A square has 4 vertices and 4 edges arranged in cycle length 4.
Each edge has exactly 2 endpoints; counting incidences by edges gives 8.
Each vertex degree is 2, so total from vertices is
\[
\sum_{v\in V}\deg(v)=2+2+2+2=8.
\]
Both counts match, proving the lemma in this case.

entries.title: Fermat's Little Theorem
entries.body:
If \(p\) is prime and \(a\in\mathbb Z\), then
\[
a^p\equiv a\pmod p.
\]
If additionally \(\gcd(a,p)=1\), then \(a^{p-1}\equiv 1\pmod p\).

entries.title: Euler-Fermat Theorem
entries.body:
If \(\gcd(a,n)=1\), then
\[
a^{\varphi(n)}\equiv 1\pmod n,
\]
where \(\varphi\) is Euler's totient.

entries.title: Dirichlet's Principle / Pigeonhole in General Form
entries.body:
If \(N\) objects are placed into \(k\) boxes, then some box contains at least
\(\left\lceil \frac{N}{k} \right\rceil\) objects.

entries.title: Eulerian Path Criterion for Finite Connected Graphs
entries.body:
A finite connected graph has an Eulerian trail iff it has 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree.
It has an Eulerian circuit iff all vertex degrees are even.

entries.title: Hall's Marriage Theorem
entries.body:
For bipartite graph \((L\cup R,E)\), there is a matching that saturates \(L\) iff for every subset \(S\subseteq L\),
\[
|N(S)|\ge |S|,
\]
where \(N(S)\) is the neighborhood of \(S\).

entries.title: Q1. Fermat's Little Theorem (Proof idea)
entries.body:
If \(p\) is prime and \(\gcd(a,p)=1\), then multiplication by \(a\) permutes residue classes \(\{1,2,\dots,p-1\}\), so
\[
\prod_{k=1}^{p-1}k \equiv \prod_{k=1}^{p-1}ak = a^{p-1}(p-1)! \pmod p.
\]
Since \((p-1)!\) has inverse mod \(p\), get \(a^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod p\). Multiplying by \(a\) gives \(a^p\equiv a\pmod p\).

entries.title: Q2. Euler-Fermat (Proof idea)
entries.body:
Consider reduced residue system mod \(n\), numbers \(a_1,\dots,a_{\varphi(n)}\) coprime to \(n\). Multiply by \(a\) with \(\gcd(a,n)=1\): residues permute the same set modulo \(n\).
Hence
\[
a_1a_2\cdots a_{\varphi(n)}\equiv (a a_1)(a a_2)\cdots(a a_{\varphi(n)})=a^{\varphi(n)}\prod_{i}a_i \pmod n.
\]
Cancel product to conclude \(a^{\varphi(n)}\equiv1\pmod n\).

entries.title: Q3. Dirichlet Principle (Proof idea)
entries.body: Assume every box has at most \(\lceil N/k\rceil-1\). Then total objects \(<k\cdot\lceil N/k\rceil\). If \(N\) does not divide \(k\), this still can be too small only if all boxes satisfy this strict upper bound; but by definition of ceiling, this contradicts pigeonhole count. Therefore some box has at least \(\lceil N/k\rceil\).

entries.title: Q4. Eulerian Trail Criterion (Proof idea)
entries.body: Each edge contributes 2 to total degree. In a trail that uses all edges exactly once, every time edges enter a vertex there is a matching exit, except possibly endpoints. Thus odd-degree vertices can only be 0 (closed circuit) or 2 (open trail). Connectivity and these degree conditions are also sufficient by repeatedly following unused edges and splicing cycles.

entries.title: Q5. Hall's Marriage Theorem (Forward direction idea)
entries.body:
Assume a perfect matching saturating \(L\) exists. Then each \(v\in S\subseteq L\) matches to a distinct vertex in \(N(S)\), so \(|N(S)|\ge|S|\).
The reverse direction (sufficiency) constructs matching via augmenting-path argument or network flow; under \(|N(S)|\ge|S|\) for all \(S\), no blocking sets remain, so augmenting algorithm finds full matching.

\\) encoding a sequence \(a_n\).

entries.title: Eulerian Circuit

entries.title: Strongly Connected
entries.body: a directed graph in which every vertex is reachable from every other via directed paths.

entries.title: Tree
entries.body: a connected graph with no cycles.

entries.title: Spanning Tree

entries.body: A directed graph with no directed cycles.

entries.title: Topological Sort

entries.title: Pigeonhole Principle

entries.title: Regular Language

entries.title: Generating Function

A **generating function** encodes sequence 


$(a_n)$


as 


$G(x)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nx^n$.

entries.title: Finite Automaton
entries.body:
A **finite automaton** is a 5-tuple 


$(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)$ with finite states 


$Q$, alphabet 


$\Sigma$, transition function 


$\delta$, start 


$\delta,q_0$, and accepting set 


$F$.

entries.title: Regular Language
entries.body: A language is **regular** iff recognized by a finite automaton.

entries.title: Context-Free Language
entries.body:
A language is **context-free** if it is generated by a context-free grammar 


$G=(V,\Sigma,R,S)$.

entries.title: NP-Complete
entries.body:
A decision problem is **NP-complete** when it is in 


$\text{NP}$


and every problem in 


$\text{NP}$


reduces to it in polynomial time.

entries.title: Burnside's Lemma
entries.body:
For finite group action 


$G\curvearrowright X$,


the number of orbits is


\[
|X/G|=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}|\mathrm{Fix}(g)|.

\]

entries.title: Pólya Enumeration
entries.body: Pólya enumeration uses cycle index polynomials to count distinct colorings under symmetries.

entries.title: Möbius Inversion
entries.body:
For arithmetic functions 


$f,g$


with 


$f(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}g(d)$, we have


\[

g(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)f(n/d).

\]

entries.title: Inclusion–Exclusion for n Sets
entries.body:
For finite sets 


$A_1,\dots,A_n$,



\[
\left|\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i\right|=\sum_{k\ge1}(-1)^{k+1}\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}|A_{i_1}\cap\cdots\cap A_{i_k}|.

\]

entries.title: Catalan Numbers
entries.body:
The 


$n$th 


Catalan number


\(C_n\)


counts balanced combinatorial structures and is


\[


C_n=\frac{1}{n+1}{2n\choose n},\quad n\ge0.

\]

entries.title: Prüfer Sequence
entries.body:
A **Prüfer sequence** is a length-


$(n-2)$


sequence of labels from 


$\{1,\dots,n\}$


encoding a labeled tree on 


$n\) vertices.

entries.title: Cayley Formula
entries.body:
The number of labeled trees on 


$n$ 


vertices is 


$n^{n-2}$.

entries.title: Planar Graph
entries.body: A graph is **planar** if it can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings.

entries.title: Euler Characteristic
entries.body:
For connected planar graph, 


$V-E+F=2$.

entries.title: Graph Coloring
entries.body:
A **proper coloring** of graph 


$G=(V,E)$


assigns colors to vertices so adjacent vertices differ.

entries.title: Random Graph
entries.body:
A **random graph** on 


$n$ vertices, typically denoted 


$G(n,p)$, has each edge present independently with probability 


$p$.

entries.title: Expectation Linearity
entries.body:
For random variables 


$X_i$, 


\(\mathbb E[\sum_i X_i]=\sum_i\mathbb EX_i\), regardless of dependence.

entries.title: Markov Chain
entries.body:
A **Markov chain** is a stochastic process with transition probabilities 


$P(X_{t+1}=j\mid X_t=i)=p_{ij}$.

entries.title: Random Walk on a Graph
entries.body:
A random walk on graph 


$G=(V,E)$ updates current vertex by choosing random neighboring vertices via transition matrix.

entries.title: Monte Carlo Method
entries.body:
A **Monte Carlo method** uses repeated random sampling to estimate quantities 


\(\mathbb E[f(X)]\n\approx \frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^N f(X_k)\).

entries.title: Big-Oh Complexity
entries.body: \(f(n)=O(g(n))\) means there exist \(C,n_0>0\) such that \(f(n)\le C g(n)\) for all \(n\ge n_0\).

entries.title: Polynomial Reduction
entries.body: A problem \(A\) reduces to \(B\) in polynomial time if an instance of \(A\) can be mapped to one of \(B\) by a polynomial-time computable function preserving yes/no answers.

entries.title: NP-Intermediate
entries.body: A language is in **NP-intermediate** if it lies in \(\mathrm{NP}\) but is neither in \(\mathrm{P}\) nor NP-complete (assuming \(\mathrm{P}\neq\mathrm{NP}\)).

entries.title: Counting Problem #P
entries.body: Class \(#\mathrm P\) contains counts of accepting paths of NP machines; e.g., number of satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula.

entries.title: Randomized Approximation Scheme
entries.body: A **FPRAS** is a randomized algorithm giving \((1\pm\epsilon)\)-approximation in time polynomial in input size and \(1/\epsilon\).

entries.title: Union Bound
entries.body:
For events \(A_1,\dots,A_n\),
\[
\Pr\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i\right)\le\sum_{i=1}^n\Pr(A_i).
\]

entries.title: Linearity of Expectation
entries.body:
For random variables \(X_i\),
\[
\mathbb E\left[\sum_i X_i\right]=\sum_i\mathbb E[X_i].
\]

entries.title: Markov Inequality
entries.body:
If \(X\ge0\) then for \(a>0\),
\[
\Pr(X\ge a)\le \frac{\mathbb E[X]}a.
\]

entries.title: Chebyshev Inequality
entries.body:
For \(\sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}(X)\) and \(k>0\),
\[
\Pr(|X-\mu|\ge k\sigma)\le\frac1{k^2}.
\]

entries.title: Martingale
entries.body:
A sequence \((X_n,\mathcal F_n)\) is a **martingale** if \(\mathbb E[|X_n|]<\infty\), is adapted, and
\[
\mathbb E[X_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=X_n.
\]

entries.title: Linearity of Expectation
entries.body:
For random variables \(X_1,\dots,X_n\),
\[
E\left[\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\right]=\sum_{i=1}^n E[X_i].
\]
No independence assumption is needed.

entries.title: Union Bound
entries.body:
For events \(E_1,\dots,E_m\),
\[\Pr\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m E_i\right)\le\sum_{i=1}^m\Pr(E_i).\]

entries.title: Lovász Local Lemma
entries.body: If events are sparse-dependent and \(P(E_i)\le p\) with neighborhood size \(d\), then under suitable conditions, all events can avoid simultaneously with nonzero probability.

entries.title: Randomized Rounding
entries.body: Given fractional solution \(x\in[0,1]^n\), convert to integral vector by setting each bit \(X_i=1\) with probability \(x_i\).

entries.title: Probabilistic Existence
entries.body:
To prove existence of a combinatorial object, show 
\(P(\text{bad event})<1\), so a good object must exist.

entries.title: Linearity of Variance
entries.body:
For pairwise uncorrelated variables,
\[
\mathrm{Var}\left(\sum_i X_i\right)=\sum_i \mathrm{Var}(X_i).
\]

entries.title: Chernoff Bound
entries.body:
For \(X=\sum_i X_i\) Bernoulli-sum and \(\delta>0\),
\[
\Pr[X>(1+\delta)\mathbb E[X]]\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{\delta^2\mathbb E[X]}{2+\delta}\right).
\]

entries.title: Randomized Algorithm
entries.body: An algorithm that makes random choices internally and succeeds with probability at least \(p>0\) (repeat to amplify success).

entries.title: Probabilistic Method
entries.body: To prove existence, show that \(\Pr(\text{failure})<1\), then a favorable object must exist.

entries.title: Monte Carlo vs Las Vegas
entries.body: Monte Carlo algorithms have bounded runtime with possible error; Las Vegas algorithms are exact when they terminate.

entries.title: Markov's Inequality
entries.body:
For nonnegative \(X\) and \(a>0\),
\[
\Pr(X\ge a)\le \frac{\mathbb E[X]}{a}.
\]

entries.title: Cantelli's Inequality
entries.body:
If \(\mathbb E[X]=0\) and \(\sigma^2=\mathrm{Var}(X)\), then for \(t>0\),
\[
\Pr(X\ge t)\le \frac{\sigma^2}{\sigma^2+t^2}.
\]

entries.title: Janson Inequality
entries.body: An upper-tail bound for sums of dependent Bernoulli variables via a dependency graph parameter \(\Delta\).

entries.title: Entropy Method in Combinatorics
entries.body: Use entropy \(H(X)\) and subadditivity to bound numbers of combinatorial configurations.

entries.title: Concentration of Measure
entries.body: Lipschitz functions on high-dimensional products are tightly concentrated around expectation, often with Gaussian-type tails.

entries.title: Martingale
entries.body: A sequence \((X_k)\) is a martingale wrt filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\) if \(E[|X_k|]<\infty\), \(X_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and \(E[X_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=X_k\).

entries.title: Azuma--Hoeffding Inequality
entries.body:
If \(X_k\) has bounded differences \(|X_k-X_{k-1}|\le c_k\), then
\[
\Pr(|X_n-X_0|\ge t)\le 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2}\right).
\]

entries.title: Doob Decomposition
entries.body: Any submartingale \(X_n\) can be uniquely decomposed as martingale part plus predictable increasing process.

entries.title: Optional Stopping
entries.body:
Under regularity, for martingale \(M_n\) and stopping time \(\tau\),
\(E[M_\tau]=E[M_0]\).

entries.title: McDiarmid's Inequality
entries.body:
For function with bounded coordinate sensitivity \(c_i\):
\[
\Pr(f- E[f]\ge t)\le \exp\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum c_i^2}\right).
\]

entries.title: Large Deviation Principle
entries.body:
A family\(X_n\) satisfies LDP with rate function \(I\) if
\[
\Pr(X_n\in A)\approx \exp\{-n\inf_{x\in A}I(x)\}.
\]

entries.title: Cramér's Theorem
entries.body: For i.i.d. \(X_i\), empirical means satisfy LDP with Legendre transform of log-mgf as rate function.

entries.title: Chernoff Bound (Moment Form)
entries.body:
For \(\lambda>0\),
\[
\Pr(X\ge t)\le\inf_{\lambda>0} e^{-\lambda t}E[e^{\lambda X}].
\]

entries.title: Vapnik-Chervonenkis Dimension
entries.body: \(\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal H)=\) largest shattered finite set size; controls uniform convergence rates.

entries.title: Sanov's Theorem
entries.body: For empirical measure \(\hat\mu_n\) of i.i.d. samples, deviations obey rate \(D(\nu\|\mu)\), the KL-divergence.

entries.title: Bounded Differences Inequality
entries.body:
If \(X=f(X_1,\dots,X_n)\) with \(|X(X_1,\dots,x_i,\dots)-X(X_1,\dots,x'_i,\dots)|\le c_i\),
then
\[
\Pr\{|X-E[X]|\ge t\}\le2\exp\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum c_i^2}\right).
\]

entries.title: Paley--Zygmund Inequality
entries.body:
For nonnegative \(X\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\),
\[
\Pr(X\ge\theta E[X])\ge (1-\theta)^2\frac{E[X]^2}{E[X^2]}.
\]

entries.title: Efron--Stein Inequality
entries.body:
For \(X= f(X_1,\dots,X_n)\),
\[
\mathrm{Var}(X)\le \frac12\sum_{i=1}^n E\big[(X-X^{(i)})^2\big],
\]
where \(X^{(i)}\) replaces only coordinate \(i\).

entries.title: Talagrand Convex Distance
entries.body: For set \(A\subseteq\Omega^n\), Talagrand distance lower-bounds concentration via convex functional on Hamming perturbations.

entries.title: Russo--Margulis Formula
entries.body:
For monotone boolean\(f\),
\[
\frac{d}{dp}E_p[f]=\sum_i \Pr_p[\partial_i f=1],
\]
where \(\partial_i f\) is edge influence at coordinate \(i\).

entries.title: Method of Conditional Expectation
entries.body: Given random variable \(X\), one derandomizes by fixing variables one-by-one while preserving \(E[X]\), yielding a deterministic object.

entries.title: Pairwise Independent Spaces
entries.body: A distribution is pairwise independent if every pair of coordinates is independent, a weaker notion useful in pseudorandom constructions.

entries.title: Nisan-Wigderson Generator
entries.body: A pseudorandom generator based on hard functions expands short seeds to fool small circuits.

entries.title: k-Wise Independence
entries.body: A family is \(k\)-wise independent if every subset of \(k\) variables has joint distribution equal to product.

entries.title: Small-Bias Spaces
entries.body: A \(\varepsilon\)-biased space makes parity tests close to unbiased while using short seeds.

entries.title: Ramsey Number
entries.body: The Ramsey number \(R(s,t)\) is smallest \(n\) such that any red-blue coloring of \(K_n\) contains a red \(K_s\) or blue \(K_t\).

entries.title: Erdős–Szekeres Bound
entries.body:
For \(R(k,k)\),
\(
2^{k/2}\le R(k,k)\le 4^k,
\)
with classical probabilistic and counting arguments.

entries.title: Turán Density
entries.body:
For \(k\)-uniform hypergraph family \(\mathcal F\), Turán density
\(\pi(\mathcal F)\) is supremum edge density avoiding copies of \(\mathcal F\).

entries.title: Hypergraph Container Theorem
entries.body: A container theorem gives a small collection of "containers" that includes all independent sets, enabling counting in sparse random structures.

entries.title: Threshold Function
entries.body:
For monotone property \(\mathcal P\) on \(G(n,p)\), threshold \(p(n)\) satisfies
\(\Pr[G(n,p)\in\mathcal P]\to 0\) below and \(\to1\) above this scaling.

entries.title: Hall's Marriage Theorem
entries.body:
In bipartite \(G=(L,R,E)\), a matching saturating \(L\) exists iff every \(S\subseteq L\) satisfies
\[
|N(S)|\ge|S|.
\]

entries.title: Sperner Theorem
entries.body: Among subsets of \([n]\), the largest antichain has size \(\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\).

entries.title: Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorem
entries.body:
For \(n\ge 2r\), the largest intersecting family \(\mathcal F\subseteq \binom{[n]}{r}\) has
\[
|\mathcal F|\le \binom{n-1}{r-1}.
\]

entries.title: Hales-Jewett Theorem
entries.body: For every \(k,m\), some \(N\) ensures every \(m\)-coloring of \([k]^N\) contains a monochromatic combinatorial line.

entries.title: Szemerédi Theorem
entries.body: If \(\delta>0\), then for sufficiently large \(n\), every subset \(A\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}\) with \(|A|\ge\delta n\) contains arithmetic progressions of any fixed length.

entries.title: Lovász Local Lemma
entries.body: For events \(A_i\), if \(\Pr(A_i)\le p\), each event depends on at most \(d\) others, and \(ep(d+1)\le1\), then \(\Pr(\bigcap\overline{A_i})>0\).

entries.title: Chernoff Bound
entries.body: For \(X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\) independent Bernoulli, \(\Pr(|X-\mu|>\delta\mu)\le 2e^{-c\delta^2\mu}\) for \(0<\delta<1\).

entries.title: Janson's Inequality
entries.body: For monotone decreasing events in dependency graph settings, \(\Pr(X\le (1-\delta)\mu)\) has exponential upper bounds involving pairwise correlation terms.

entries.title: Erdos-Rényi Random Graph
entries.body: The graph \(G(n,p)\) has \(n\) labeled vertices with each edge included independently with probability \(p\).

entries.title: Threshold Phenomenon
entries.body: For a graph property \(\mathcal P\), a threshold \(p_0(n)\) satisfies transition from \(\Pr[G(n,p)\in \mathcal P]\to0\) to \(\to1\) as \(p\) crosses \(p_0\).

entries.title: Sample Space
entries.body: A **sample space** is the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment, typically denoted \(\Omega\).

entries.title: Event
entries.body: An **event** is any subset of \(\Omega\) that is in the associated sigma-algebra.

entries.title: Probability Measure
entries.body:
A function 
\(\mathbb P:\mathcal F\to[0,1]\) with 
\(\mathbb P(\Omega)=1\), nonnegativity, and countable additivity.

entries.title: Conditional Probability
entries.body:
For events 
\(A,B\) with
\(\mathbb P(B)>0\):
\[
\mathbb P(A\mid B)=\frac{\mathbb P(A\cap B)}{\mathbb P(B)}.
\]

entries.title: Bayes' Theorem
entries.body:
For partition 
\((B_i)_{i}\) with 
\(\mathbb P(B_i)>0\),
\[
\mathbb P(B_k\mid A)=\frac{\mathbb P(A\mid B_k)\mathbb P(B_k)}{\sum_i\mathbb P(A\mid B_i)\mathbb P(B_i)}.
\]

entries.title: Random Variable
entries.body:
A measurable map 
\(X:(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to(E,\mathcal E)\), often 
\(\mathbb R\) with Borel sigma-algebra.

entries.title: Probability Mass Function
entries.body:
For discrete 
\(X\), 
\(p_X(x)=\mathbb P(X=x)\) with 
\(\sum_x p_X(x)=1\).

entries.title: Expectation
entries.body:
For discrete 
\(X\), 
\[
\mathbb E[X]=\sum_x x\,p_X(x).
\]

entries.title: Probability Density Function
entries.body:
A function 
\(f_X\) for continuous 
\(X\) such that 
\(\mathbb P(a\le X\le b)=\int_a^b f_X(x)\,dx\).

entries.title: Cumulative Distribution Function
entries.body:
\[
F_X(x)=\mathbb P(X\le x).
\]

entries.title: Moment Generating Function
entries.body:
\[
M_X(t)=\mathbb E[e^{tX}],
\]
when finite in neighborhood of 
\(t=0\).

entries.title: Bernoulli Distribution
entries.body:
\(X\sim\mathrm{Bern}(p)\) has 
\(\mathbb P(X=1)=p\), 
\(\mathbb P(X=0)=1-p\).

entries.title: Binomial Distribution
entries.body:
\(X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\):
\[
\mathbb P(X=k)=\binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}.
\]

entries.title: Normal Distribution
entries.body:
\(X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)\) with density
\[
f_X(x)=\frac1{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).
\]

entries.title: Law of Large Numbers
entries.body:
If 
\(X_i\) are i.i.d. with mean 
\(\mu\), sample average
\(\bar X_n\to\mu\) in probability.

entries.title: Central Limit Theorem
entries.body:
If 
\(X_i\) i.i.d. with mean 
\(\mu\), variance 
\(\sigma^2\),
\[
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i-n\mu}{\sigma\sqrt n}\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal N(0,1).
\]

entries.title: Likelihood Function
entries.body:
For data 
\(x\), parameter 
\(\theta\):
\(L(\theta\mid x)=p(x\mid\theta)\).

entries.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimator
entries.body:
An MLE 
\(\hat\theta_{\mathrm{MLE}}\) maximizes 
\(L(\theta\mid x)\) (or log-likelihood).

entries.title: Unbiased Estimator
entries.body:
Estimator 
\(\hat\theta\) is unbiased if
\(\mathbb E[\hat\theta]=\theta\).

entries.title: Null and Alternative Hypotheses
entries.body:
Statistical test compares 
\(H_0\) vs 
\(H_1\).

entries.title: p-Value
entries.body:
For test statistic 
\(T\), p-value is the null-tail probability of outcomes at least as extreme as observed.

entries.title: Markov Chain
entries.body:
A stochastic process 
\(X_t\) with
\[\mathbb P(X_{t+1}=j\mid X_t=i,X_{t-1},\dots)=\mathbb P(X_{t+1}=j\mid X_t=i).
\]

entries.title: Stationary Distribution
entries.body:
A distribution 
\(\pi\) is stationary if
\(\pi P=\pi\) for transition matrix 
\(P\).

entries.title: Brownian Motion
entries.body:
A process 
\((W_t)\) with continuous paths, independent increments, and
\(W_{t+s}-W_t\sim\mathcal N(0,s)\).

entries.title: Ito Integral
entries.body:
For adapted process 
\(X_t\),
\[\int_0^T X_t\,dW_t\]
is defined in mean-square (Itô) sense.

entries.title: Risk-Neutral Probability
entries.body: A probability measure \(\mathbb Q\) such that discounted asset prices are martingales.

entries.title: Random Walk
entries.body:
A process 
\(S_n=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\) for i.i.d. increments 
\(X_i\).

entries.title: Covariance
entries.body:
\[
\mathrm{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[(X-\mu_X)(Y-\mu_Y)].
\]

entries.title: Correlation
entries.body:
\[
\rho_{XY}=\frac{\mathrm{Cov}(X,Y)}{\sigma_X\sigma_Y},\quad |\rho_{XY}|\le1.
\]

entries.title: Poisson Distribution
entries.body:
\[\mathbb P(N=n)=\frac{\lambda^n e^{-\lambda}}{n!},\quad n\in\mathbb N_0.
\]

entries.title: Entropy
entries.body:
\[
H(X)=-\sum_x p_X(x)\log p_X(x).
\]

entries.title: Variance
entries.body:
The variance of \(X\) is
\[
\mathrm{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[(X-\mu)^2],\quad \mu=\mathbb E[X].
\]

entries.title: Standard Deviation
entries.body: Standard deviation is \(\sigma_X=\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(X)}\), the scale of spread in same units as \(X\).

entries.title: Covariance Matrix
entries.body:
For \(X\in\mathbb R^d\), covariance matrix is
\[
\Sigma_{ij}=\mathrm{Cov}(X_i,X_j).
\]
\(\Sigma\) is symmetric and positive semidefinite.

entries.title: Characteristic Function
entries.body:
The characteristic function of \(X\) is
\[
\varphi_X(t)=\mathbb E[e^{itX}],
\]
which uniquely determines the distribution.

entries.title: Conditional Expectation
entries.body:
Conditional expectation \( \mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal G] \) is the \( \mathcal G \)-measurable random variable minimizing mean squared error among all \(\mathcal G\)-measurable \(Y\):
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[(X-Y)^2\right]\text{ is minimized by }Y=\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal G].
\]

entries.title: Law of Total Probability
entries.body:
For disjoint events \(B_i\) partitioning \(\Omega\):
\[
\mathbb P(A)=\sum_i \mathbb P(A\mid B_i)\mathbb P(B_i).
\]

entries.title: Chebyshev Inequality
entries.body:
If \(X\) has finite mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\), then for \(k>0\):
\[
\mathbb P\big(|X-\mu|\ge k\big)\le \frac{\sigma^2}{k^2}.
\]

entries.title: Confidence Interval
entries.body:
A \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence interval for \(\theta\) is a random interval \([L(X),U(X)]\) with
\[
\mathbb P_\theta\!\left(L(X)\le \theta\le U(X)\right)\ge 1-\alpha.
\]

entries.title: Convergence in Distribution
entries.body: Sequence \(X_n\) converges in distribution to \(X\), written \(X_n\xrightarrow{d}X\), if \(\mathbb E[f(X_n)]\to\mathbb E[f(X)]\) for all bounded continuous \(f\).

entries.title: Kullback-Leibler Divergence
entries.body:
For densities \(p,q\):
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=\int p(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\,dx.
\]
It measures directed divergence and is nonnegative.

entries.title: Prior Distribution
entries.body: The prior \(p(\theta)\) expresses belief about parameter \(\theta\) before observing data.

entries.title: Posterior Distribution
entries.body:
Posterior updates prior using data \(x\):
\[
p(\theta\mid x)\propto p(x\mid\theta)\,p(\theta).
\]

entries.title: Maximum A Posteriori
entries.body:
MAP estimate:
\[
\hat\theta_{\mathrm{MAP}}=\arg\max_\theta p(\theta\mid x).
\]
It is the mode of posterior \(p(\theta\mid x)\).

entries.title: Stationary Process
entries.body: A stochastic process \((X_t)\) is (weakly) stationary when its mean is constant and covariance depends only on lag.

entries.title: Autocovariance
entries.body:
For lag \(h\):
\[
\gamma(h)=\mathrm{Cov}(X_t,X_{t+h}).
\]

entries.title: Autoregressive Process
entries.body:
AR(1):
\[
X_t=\phi X_{t-1}+\epsilon_t,\qquad \epsilon_t\sim\text{white noise}.
\]

entries.title: Value at Risk
entries.body:
For loss \(L\), confidence \(1-\alpha\), VaR is:
\[
\mathrm{VaR}_{\alpha}=\inf\{x:\mathbb P(L\le x)\ge 1-\alpha\}.
\]

entries.title: Conditional Value at Risk
entries.body:
\[
\mathrm{CVaR}_{\alpha}=\mathbb E[L\mid L\ge \mathrm{VaR}_{\alpha}]
\]
is the expected loss beyond VaR.

entries.title: Log-Likelihood
entries.body:
Log-likelihood for i.i.d. data \(x_i\):
\[
\ell(\theta)=\sum_i \log p(x_i\mid\theta).
\]

entries.title: Fisher Information
entries.body:
For scalar \(\theta\):
\[
\mathcal I(\theta)=\mathbb E\!\left[\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\log p(X\mid\theta)\right)^2\right].
\]

entries.title: Cramér-Rao Lower Bound
entries.body:
For unbiased \(\hat\theta\),
\[
\mathrm{Var}(\hat\theta)\ge \frac{1}{\mathcal I(\theta)}.
\]

entries.title: Bregman Divergence
entries.body:
For convex \(\phi\):
\[
D_\phi(p\|q)=\phi(p)-\phi(q)-\phi'(q)(p-q).
\]

entries.title: Monte Carlo Estimator
entries.body:
For \(\mathbb E[f(X)]\), with \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) i.i.d.,
\[
\hat\mu_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f(X_i)
\]
is unbiased if \( \mathbb E[f(X)]\) exists and converges by LLN.

entries.title: Importance Sampling
entries.body:
To estimate \(\mathbb E_p[g(X)]\) using proposal \(q\),
\[
\mathbb E_p[g(X)] = \mathbb E_q\!\left[g(X)\frac{p(X)}{q(X)}\right].
\]
Variance improves when \(q\) places more mass where \(g(X)p(X)\) is large.

entries.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo
entries.body: **MCMC** builds a Markov chain with stationary law \(\pi\) so samples are asymptotically distributed as \(\pi\), enabling expectations by averages.

entries.title: Ergodicity (Markov Chains)
entries.body: A chain is ergodic when it has a unique stationary distribution and converges to it from any start, typically via irreducible and aperiodic behavior.

entries.title: Bias
entries.body:
Bias of estimator \(\hat\theta\) for \(\theta\):
\[
\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)=\mathbb E[\hat\theta]-\theta.
\]

entries.title: Mean Squared Error
entries.body:
\[
\operatorname{MSE}(\hat\theta)=\mathbb E[(\hat\theta-\theta)^2]
=\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta)+\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)^2.
\]

entries.title: Consistency
entries.body:
An estimator \(\hat\theta_n\) is consistent for \(\theta\) if
\[
\hat\theta_n\xrightarrow{P}\theta.
\]

entries.title: Law of the Unconscious Statistician
entries.body:
For measurable \(g\) and \(X\),
\[
\mathbb E[g(X)]=\int g(x)\,dF_X(x)=\int g(x)f_X(x)\,dx.
\]

entries.title: Copula
entries.body:
A copula \(C\) couples marginal CDFs \(F_1,\dots,F_d\) into a joint CDF:
\[
F(x_1,\dots,x_d)=C(F_1(x_1),\dots,F_d(x_d)).
\]

entries.title: Tail Dependence
entries.body:
Upper-tail dependence \(\lambda_U\) between \(X,Y\):
\[
\lambda_U=\lim_{u\uparrow1}\mathbb P\!\left(Y>F_Y^{-1}(u)\mid X>F_X^{-1}(u)\right).
\]

entries.title: Student's \(t\)-Copula
entries.body: The \(t\)-copula uses a multivariate \(t\)-distribution template to model symmetric heavy-tail dependence.

entries.title: Expected Shortfall (Alternate Form)
entries.body:
For loss \(L\) and level \(\alpha\):
\[
\mathrm{ES}_\alpha = \frac{1}{\alpha}\int_0^\alpha \mathrm{VaR}_u\,du
\]
for \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).

entries.title: Martingale
entries.body:
A process \((M_t)\) adapted to filtration \((\mathcal F_t)\) is a martingale if
\[
\mathbb E[|M_t|]<\infty,\quad \mathbb E[M_t\mid\mathcal F_s]=M_s,\ \forall s\le t.
\]

entries.title: Quadratic Variation
entries.body:
For semimartingale \(X\), quadratic variation up to \(T\) is
\[
[X]_T=\lim_{\|\pi\|\to0}\sum_{i}(X_{t_i}-X_{t_{i-1}})^2.
\]

entries.title: It\^o Process
entries.body:
An It\^o process has form
\[
dX_t=\mu_t\,dt+\sigma_t\,dW_t.
\]

entries.title: Stochastic Integral
entries.body:
For adapted \(X_t\) and Brownian motion \(W_t\),
\[
\int_0^T X_t\,dW_t
\]
is defined as an \(L^2\) limit of left-point Riemann sums.

entries.title: Geometric Brownian Motion
entries.body:
GBM satisfies
\[
dS_t=\mu S_t\,dt+\sigma S_t\,dW_t,\quad S_0>0.
\]

entries.title: Risk-Neutral Measure
entries.body: Under \(\mathbb Q\), discounted asset prices become martingales and expected growth equals the risk-free rate.

entries.title: Girsanov Theorem
entries.body: Girsanov changes drift via a measure shift; under suitable Novikov conditions, Brownian motion under \(\mathbb P\) becomes Brownian with drift removed under \(\mathbb Q\).

entries.title: Black–Scholes PDE
Filtered Probability Space
entries.body: An increasing family of sigma-algebras \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}\) represents information available up to time \(t\).

entries.title: Radon--Nikodym Derivative
entries.body:
If \(Q\ll P\), then
\[
\frac{dQ}{dP}
\]
is the density giving \(Q(A)=\int_A \frac{dQ}{dP}\,dP\).

entries.title: Cross-Entropy
entries.body:
Cross-entropy of \(p\) relative to \(q\):
\[
H(p,q)=-\sum_x p(x)\log q(x).
\]

entries.title: KL to Wasserstein Link
entries.body: KL controls distribution proximity, while Wasserstein captures geometry/transport; both are used in generative model objectives.

entries.title: Bayes Risk
entries.body:
Bayes risk under decision rule \(\delta\) and prior \(\pi\) is the posterior-weighted expected loss:
\[
r_B(\delta)=\mathbb E_{\theta\sim\pi}\,\mathbb E_{X\mid\theta}\left[\ell\!\left(\delta(X),\theta\right)\right].
\]

entries.title: Expected Utility
entries.body:
An action is chosen by maximizing expected utility:
\[
\max_a \mathbb E[U(a,X)].
\]

entries.title: Regret
entries.body:
For action \(a\), expected regret is
\[
\mathrm{Regret}(a)=\mathbb E[L(a,X)]-\inf_{a'}\mathbb E[L(a',X)].
\]

entries.title: Markov Decision Process
entries.body:
An MDP is the tuple \((\mathcal S,\mathcal A,P,r,\gamma)\):
state space, action space, transition kernel, reward, and discount factor.

entries.title: Bellman Equation
entries.body:
For policy \(\pi\) with value function \(V^\pi\),
\[
V^\pi(s)=\mathbb E\!\left[r(s,a)+\gamma V^\pi(S')\mid S=s,A\sim\pi(\cdot\mid s)\right].
\]

entries.title: Q-Value Function
entries.body:
The action-value function is
\[
Q^\pi(s,a)=\mathbb E\!\left[r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{a'}\pi(a'\mid S')Q^\pi(S',a')\mid S=s,A=a\right].
\]

entries.title: Temporal Difference Error
entries.body:
At step \(t\), TD error is
\[
\delta_t=R_{t+1}+\gamma V(S_{t+1})-V(S_t).
\]

entries.title: Drawdown
entries.body:
For cumulative value \(V_t\), drawdown is
\[
\mathrm{DD}_t=\max_{0\le s\le t}V_s-V_t.
\]

entries.title: Maximum Drawdown
entries.body:
Maximum drawdown over horizon \(T\):
\[
\mathrm{MDD}=\max_{0\le t\le T}\mathrm{DD}_t.
\]

entries.title: Sharpe Ratio
entries.body:
For return mean \(\mu\), risk-free rate \(r_f\), and volatility \(\sigma\),
\[
\mathrm{SR}=\frac{\mu-r_f}{\sigma}.
\]

entries.title: Calmar Ratio
entries.body:
Calmar ratio is return normalized by max drawdown:
\[
\mathrm{Calmar}=\frac{\text{Annualized Return}}{\mathrm{MDD}}.
\]

entries.title: Convex Risk Measure
entries.body: A map \(\rho:L^\infty\to\mathbb R\) is a convex risk measure when it satisfies monotonicity, translation invariance, and convexity in losses.

entries.title: Coherent Risk Measure
entries.body:
A coherent risk measure is a convex risk measure additionally satisfying positive homogeneity and subadditivity.
\[
\rho(X+Y)\le\rho(X)+\rho(Y),\qquad \rho(\lambda X)=\lambda\rho(X),\;\lambda\ge0.
\]

entries.title: Entropic Risk Measure
entries.body:
For \(\theta>0\),
\[
\rho_\theta(X)=\frac1\theta\log\mathbb E[e^{\theta X}]
\]
penalizes tail events with exponential weighting.

entries.title: Conditional Value at Risk as Optimization
entries.body:
CVaR admits dual form
\[
\mathrm{CVaR}_\alpha(X)=\min_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\left\{\eta+\frac1\alpha\mathbb E[(X-\eta)_+]\right\}.
\]

entries.title: Mean-Variance Frontier
entries.body:
The set of admissible portfolios \((\mu,\sigma^2)\) generated by
\[
\min_w w^\top\Sigma w\quad\text{subject to}\quad \mu^\top w=\mu_0,\; \mathbf 1^\top w=1.
\]
defines the efficient frontier.

entries.title: PAC-Bayesian Bound
entries.body:
For posterior \(Q\), prior \(P\), empirical risk \(\hat L\), true risk \(L\), and \(n\) samples:
\[
L(Q)\le \hat L(Q)+\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)+\log(2\sqrt n/\delta)}{2(n-1)}}.
\]

entries.title: Rademacher Complexity
entries.body:
For class \(\mathcal F\), sample \(x_1,\dots,x_n\), and Rademacher signs \(\sigma_i\):
\[
\hat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal F)=\mathbb E_\sigma\left[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i f(x_i)\right].
\]

entries.title: VC Dimension
entries.body: VC dimension is the largest \(d\) such that some set of \(d\) points is shattered by a hypothesis class.

entries.title: Information Bottleneck Objective
entries.body:
Given encoder \(p(z\mid x)\), objective trades compression and prediction:
\[
\mathcal L=\mathbb E[-\log q(y\mid z)]+\beta\,I(X;Z).
\]

entries.title: ARCH Process
entries.body:
In ARCH(\(q\)):
\[
r_t=\mu+\epsilon_t,\qquad \epsilon_t=\sigma_t z_t,\qquad \sigma_t^2=\alpha_0+\sum_{i=1}^q\alpha_i\epsilon_{t-i}^2.
\]

entries.title: GARCH Process
entries.body:
In GARCH(\(p,q\)):
\[
\sigma_t^2=\alpha_0+\sum_{i=1}^q\alpha_i\epsilon_{t-i}^2+\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_j\sigma_{t-j}^2.
\]

entries.title: Stochastic Volatility
entries.body:
Model with latent log-variance:
\[
h_t=\phi h_{t-1}+\eta_t,\quad r_t=\exp(h_t/2)\, \epsilon_t.
\]

entries.title: Hurst Exponent
entries.body:
The Hurst exponent \(H\in(0,1)\) measures long-range dependence:
\[
H<0.5:\text{mean-reverting},\quad H=0.5:\text{random walk},\quad H>0.5:\text{persistent}.
\]

entries.title: CUSUM Statistic
entries.body:
For target \(\mu_0\), cumulative sum detection uses
\[
S_t=\sum_{i=1}^t (X_i-\mu_0).
\]
A change is flagged when \(S_t\) crosses decision boundaries.

entries.title: Likelihood Ratio Test
entries.body:
For hypotheses \(H_0,H_1\) and data \(x\):
\[
\Lambda(x)=\frac{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_0}L(\theta\mid x)}{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_1}L(\theta\mid x)}.
\]
Reject \(H_0\) when \(\Lambda(x)\) is sufficiently small.

entries.title: Recursive Bayesian Filtering
entries.body:
For latent state \(X_t\) and observation \(Y_t\):
\[
p(x_t\mid y_{1:t})\propto p(y_t\mid x_t)\int p(x_t\mid x_{t-1})p(x_{t-1}\mid y_{1:t-1})dx_{t-1}.
\]

entries.title: Kalman Filter
entries.body: For linear-Gaussian state-space models, the filter updates posterior state mean and covariance with a prediction step and an innovation correction.

entries.title: Robust Estimator
entries.body: An estimator is robust if it is not overly sensitive to small amounts of contamination or outliers.

entries.title: Influence Function
entries.body:
For estimator \(T\) at distribution \(F\), influence function is
\[
\mathrm{IF}(z;T,F)=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}T((1-\epsilon)F+\epsilon\Delta_z)\right|_{\epsilon=0}.
\]

entries.title: Huber Loss
entries.body:
\[
\rho_\delta(u)=
\begin{cases}
\frac12u^2,& |u|\le\delta,\\
\delta|u|-\frac12\delta^2,& |u|>\delta.
\end{cases}
\]

entries.title: Adversarial Robustness Margin
entries.body: The maximum perturbation radius \(\epsilon\) for which model output remains unchanged under \(\|\eta\|_\infty\le\epsilon\).

entries.title: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
entries.body: HMC simulates Hamiltonian dynamics on an expanded state space (position+momentum) to build long-distance MCMC proposals with high acceptance.

entries.title: Gibbs Sampler
entries.body: Gibbs sampling updates blocks from full conditionals: draw each parameter block from \(p(\theta_i\mid\theta_{-i},x)\).

entries.title: Variational Bayes
entries.body:
VB solves an optimization problem over tractable families \(\mathcal Q\):
\[
q^*=\arg\min_{q\in\mathcal Q}\mathrm{KL}(q(\theta)\|p(\theta\mid x)).
\]

entries.title: Effective Sample Size
entries.body:
For autocorrelated draws, effective sample size is
\[
n_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{n}{1+2\sum_{k\ge1}\rho_k}.
\]

entries.title: Extreme-Value Index
entries.body: For tail cdf \( \bar F(x)=1-F(x) \), the extreme-value index \(\xi\) characterizes tail decay and dictates whether tails are heavy (\(\xi>0\)), light (\(\xi=0\)), or bounded (\(\xi<0\)).

entries.title: Block Maxima
entries.body: Divide observations into blocks of size \(m\); maxima \(M_j=\max\{X_{(j-1)m+1},\dots,X_{jm}\}\) are used to fit a GEV model.

entries.title: Generalized Extreme Value Distribution
entries.body:
With location \(\mu\), scale \(\sigma>0\), and shape \(\xi\):
\[
G_{\mu,\sigma,\xi}(x)=\exp\left[-\left(1+\xi\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^{-1/\xi}\right],\quad 1+\xi\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}>0.
\]
At \(\xi\to0\), this converges to the Gumbel form \( \exp(-e^{-z}) \) with \(z=(x-\mu)/\sigma\).

entries.title: Pickands–Balkema–de Haan Theorem
entries.body:
For high threshold \(u\), exceedance tails satisfy
\[
\sup_{0\le y\le y_{\max}}\left| \Pr(X-u\le y\mid X>u)-G_{\xi,\beta}(y)\right|\to 0,
\]
where \(G_{\xi,\beta}\) is a Generalized Pareto distribution.

entries.title: Generalized Pareto Distribution
entries.body:
Tail of \(Y=X-u\mid X>u\):
\[
\Pr(Y>y)=\left(1+\frac{\xi y}{\beta}\right)^{-1/\xi},\quad y\ge0,\;1+\frac{\xi y}{\beta}>0.
\]

entries.title: Wasserstein Distance
entries.body:
For \(p\ge1\), transport cost \(c(x,y)=\|x-y\|^p\):
\[
W_p(\mu,\nu)=\left(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int \|x-y\|^p\,d\pi(x,y)\right)^{1/p}.
\]
\(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) is the set of couplings with marginals \(\mu,\nu\).

entries.title: Kantorovich-Rubinstein Duality
entries.body:
For \(p=1\):
\[
W_1(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le1}\left(\int f\,d\mu-\int f\,d\nu\right).
\]

entries.title: Maximum Mean Discrepancy
entries.body:
With kernel \(k\) and feature map in RKHS \(\mathcal H\):
\[
\mathrm{MMD}^2(P,Q)=\mathbb E_{x,x'\sim P}k(x,x')+\mathbb E_{y,y'\sim Q}k(y,y')-2\mathbb E_{x\sim P,y\sim Q}k(x,y).
\]

entries.title: Entropic Regularized Optimal Transport
entries.body:
The entropy-regularized objective is
\[
\min_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int c(x,y)\,d\pi(x,y)+\varepsilon\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|P\otimes Q).
\]
This formulation is used in differentiable transport matching (Sinkhorn-type algorithms).

entries.title: Lévy Process
entries.body:
A Lévy process \((L_t)\) has stationary independent increments, càdlàg paths, and characteristic exponent \(\psi\) with
\[
\mathbb E[e^{iuL_t}]=e^{t\psi(u)}.
\]

entries.title: Jump-Diffusion Model
entries.body:
An asset model with jumps has SDE
\[
dS_t=\mu S_{t-}\,dt+\sigma S_{t-}\,dW_t+S_{t-}\,dJ_t,
\]
where \(J_t\) is a pure-jump process (often compound Poisson).

entries.title: Variance Gamma Process
entries.body:
VG can be represented as Brownian motion with drift evaluated at random gamma time:
\[
X_t=\theta G_t+\sigma W_{G_t},\qquad G_t\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(t,\nu).
\]

entries.title: Policy Gradient Theorem
entries.body:
For return \(J(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\sum_t r_t\right]\):
\[
\nabla_\theta J(\theta)=
\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\sum_t\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(A_t\mid S_t)\,G_t\right].
\]
